# Homeplot — Development Plan (Main Reference Doc)

**This is THE main development plan.** Every future Claudia dispatch and every future planning conversation should start here. It supersedes the earlier one-off `Homeplot_Development_Plan.pdf` (generated once, sent to the teacher, never stored in the repo — the exact problem this file exists to fix: a doc Claudia is told to "reference" has to actually live somewhere Claudia can read it on every dispatch, not a PDF that only ever reached the teacher's inbox).

**Built for:** K-8 students with high support needs (autism, ADHD, dyslexia, communication disorders).
**Owner/teacher:** Kayden, Vermont Literacy Network.
**Stack:** React + React Three Fiber (3D world), Zustand + Supabase (Postgres, Storage, realtime sync), Vercel (hosting, auto-deploy on push to `main`).

Shipped (A46). |

**How to use this doc with Claudia:** Part A is what already exists (build on it or revise it explicitly, don't re-propose it). Part B is the open backlog, organized by feature front, each pointing at its own doc where one exists — the best place to start a gameplay-design conversation. Part C is the teacher's own raw notes on the pets system and platformer, preserved close to verbatim. Part D is the standing design/safety/accessibility rules every new feature gets checked against.

## 🧱 BUILD QUEUE: what gets built next, in order

**Her standing rule (2026-10-09, verbatim):** "claudia, continue with all queued items, always add items to a queue list and work through them until completed".

**Live tracker for her (2026-10-15, Build Queue 202: "keep queue updted and presentable to me so i can keep track"):** https://claude.ai/artifact/Xj955Dv7fySwuXA4emGxAe, built from this section by `scripts/build-queue-page.py` and republished after every push to main (Working on now, Up next in order, Waiting on you, Done today, Done earlier).

How it works: every new request, idea or "queue:" message goes on this list the same turn it arrives. Work goes top to bottom, each item ships on its own (dev plan, What's New if students notice it, push to main), then it moves to **Done** with its date. An item that needs her answer moves to "Waiting on the teacher" below instead of blocking the line. Full detail for each item lives in its own entry (Gameplay roadmap, section 2).

96. 🧪 **Supernature (was the Potion Lab): its own app, split from the Science Lab.** IN PROGRESS: FIRST MODEL LIVE 2026-10-13 (see Part A, A57). **Biome views, pixel Ocean, potions only in Supernature (Build Queue 123 to 126, shipped 2026-10-13):** side arrows move between six views including an underwater Ocean with an animated pixel surface; creatures are assigned biomes and each biome changes their reactions; the note moved to the title bar and the right buttons are icons; potions no longer work outside Supernature; Habitat art is all pixel. **Four seasons, season potions and a bigger Shop (Build Queue 120 to 122, shipped 2026-10-13):** the Habitat runs real 10 minute seasons on a clock every device shares (1 minute days and nights, 5 of each), with a moving sun, season art and sounds, season reactions, baby seasons, survival at the end of each season and leveling up after all four; 11 season potions with exact jobs; 40 more Shop ingredients on five shelves. **Habitat dock, potion hotbar and reactions (Build Queue 117 and 118, shipped 2026-10-13):** a bottom dock with picture tiles for Land, Time, Weather, Disaster and Surprises (each opens a sideways scrolling tray of cards that say what the choice does), a nine-slot potion hotbar with pixel bottles and counts (tap then tap a glowing creature, or drag onto it; empty slots offer Brew one), and a Take cover tile; the season panel became a small pill and four big buttons on the right. Body features (`src/lib/supernatureAdapt.ts`) now decide every creature's reaction to each change, shown as a bubble and a pose on the creature, a Why in its card, a who-is-fine note and a How they react list. **Cauldron rework and careful tracing (Build Queue 113, shipped 2026-10-13):** no separate bowl: step 1 is now "Mix ( grass + dew ) in the cauldron first. Parentheses always go first." (the order-of-operations idea stays) and the pour step is gone. A pixel wooden stick stands in the pot and swirls twice every time something goes in. Ingredients are dragged from the shelf onto the cauldron (the pot glows while dragging), and a tap still works for students who find dragging hard. Stirring is drawing circles on the pot (each full circle is one stir, and the stick follows the finger), with a Stir once button too. Cursive tracing now needs accuracy: Done checks how much of the guide letters were covered (55% needed) and how much ink stayed on the letters (60% needed), with a live Tracing meter and a plain hint when it is not there yet (trace more of the light letters, or keep lines on the letters and try Undo line). The guide word is drawn on a canvas so the check and the letters line up exactly. **Interactive Globe (Build Queue 112, shipped 2026-10-13):** the Globe is a real world map (Natural Earth country shapes through the world-atlas package, public domain; d3-geo draws it) shown as a pixel globe. It turns slowly on its own until touched; drag to spin it any way, pinch, scroll or tap Zoom in and Zoom out (1x to 7x), Fit resets it, and Spin or Stop toggles the turning. Continent and ocean names show from far away; country names appear as you zoom in, bigger countries first. Tapping a country highlights it gold, says its name, shows which continent it is on and the creatures whose stories come from there; tapping water picks the ocean. Every creature has a pin where its story comes from (a gold ? until found, its picture after); tapping a pin shows it, and Explore flies the globe to the creature just found. The 12 continent and ocean buttons now sit above the info card and fly the globe there. **Naturalist rank, creature levels and cards (Build Queue 105 and 109, shipped 2026-10-13):** a 🏅 rank chip on Home opens the rank card: XP from creatures found (10), made (15), recipes brewed (10), Habitat seasons (5), creature levels (5) and correct energy check-ins (3), with a progress bar and the five ranks. Each rank adds something and nothing that was open gets locked: Field Scout, 6 sparkly colors in the Creature Maker; Creature Keeper, Rainbow Storm (a magic weather); Habitat Builder, Meteor Sparkles (a magic night sky); Grand Naturalist, gold card frames and a crown for the Cat Wizard. Creatures gain a level (shown as Lv by their name and in their help card) after a Balanced season with their energy at just right, and the Field Notebook announces level ups. Creature cards: a 🃏 button on every Encyclopedia page and a My cards button on the Contents page open a collectible card (chapter color frame, picture, Lv, origin, power, what it eats, energy face, and its story line), private to the student. **Potions out in the world (Build Queue 104, shipped 2026-10-13):** on the Aero or Veloaero recipe page, Drink it and go to Town Square uses one potion and opens Town Square, where the student floats above the ground for 60 seconds (Veloaero also moves almost twice as fast), with a countdown chip at the bottom ('🪽 Aero: floating, 42s'; `src/lib/potionEffects.ts`, read by the Town Square player every frame; it never applies while driving). On the Fort or Velo page, Give it to a pet lists the student's pets; one potion gives that pet +1 training through the existing trainPet, once a day per student (her answer: potions count toward training to a degree). **Be the creature (Build Queue 103, shipped 2026-10-13):** tap a creature in the Habitat, then 🎮 Be this creature, for a 90-second round in its land. Tap anywhere to walk there, or use the big joystick. Its diet is the goal: plant eaters munch plants, hunters tag prey (other Habitat creatures that eat plants; the prey runs from you and poofs safely back to its burrow), leftover eaters clean up logs and feed the soil, magic eaters gather sparkles. When there is a meat eater in the Habitat, plant eaters get chased now and then: hide in a bush and it cannot see you; getting caught just sends you back to your burrow. Energy uses her 5 faces: moving wears it down, eating lifts it, resting brings it back to just right. The summary counts what you ate, the chases, the hiding and how long your energy stayed just right, with Listen, Play again and Back to the Habitat. **Generations (Build Queue 102, shipped 2026-10-13):** a 🧬 Generations button in the Habitat's season panel opens a lab: pick a group, a trait to watch (fur, color, legs or shell, each 1 to 5) and a world (like my Habitat, much colder, much hotter, a new hunter arrives, a dark forest, snowy white land). Ten creatures start with a spread of the trait; each generation, the ones that fit the world a little better are a little more likely to have babies, and babies are like their parents with small differences. The Generations chart shows the last 8 generations as ten numbered squares each, with how many have the high trait; Next generation, a Time Machine slider (2 to 20 generations at once) and Start over. The summary keeps the science accurate ("The group evolved over 12 generations. Thick fur: 3 of 10 in generation 1, 8 of 10 in generation 13. No single creature changed its body."), and when a group has clearly changed, Name the new form opens the Name Builder. **Shop and Cookbook (Build Queue 100 and 101, shipped 2026-10-13):** the vending machine Shop sells 21 ingredients from her packs for real money from the student's bank (a register line, 'Supernature Shop: name'): basic ones $1 to $5 (eye of newt is really a mustard seed, slime core is the one gross one, never a base ingredient) and rare ones $20 to $50 (bottled moonlight, saffron, mermaid tear, phoenix feather, dragon scale, frozen flame); glass bottle, grass, dew and fairy wing stay free, and a mermaid tear or phoenix feather earned on the Globe counts as owned. Each item shows its price, a note, the recipes that use it and how many the student has. The Cookbook grew to 10 base recipes (Aero, Vita, Dorm, Viv, Lumin, Cryo, Aqua, Fort, Velo, Mega) and 3 discovered ones that unlock after their base potion is brewed (her example: Aero unlocks Veloaero, super speed flying; Vita unlocks Megavita; Cryo unlocks Pyro), shown as a locked secret until then. Bought ingredients are used up only when a potion is finished, so a fizzle never costs money; missing ones say what to buy and link to the Shop. In the Habitat: Vita heals, Dorm calms high energy, Viv wakes low energy, Mega makes a creature giant for a minute, and a Potions button holds Lumin (lights all night), Megavita (heals everyone), Cryo (puts out a wildfire), Aqua (ends a drought) and Pyro (ends a blizzard). Aero, Veloaero, Fort and Velo work outside Supernature next (Build Queue 104). **Also fixed:** the root `npx tsc --noEmit` checks no files in this project (its tsconfig only lists references), so CLAUDE.md now says `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json`, which does. **Food web and seasons (Build Queue 99, shipped 2026-10-13):** every creature now has what it eats on its Encyclopedia page (plants, meat, both, leftovers as scavengers, or magic; made creatures use their Maker diet). In the Habitat each creature is a group (shown as ×3 by its name). A season panel in the top right shows the season, plants and mushrooms, with Food web and Next season. Next season asks for a prediction first (pick a group, then more, the same or fewer), then runs: plants grow by land, weather and season; plant eaters eat; hunters catch plant eaters, who run back to their burrows (a poof, the group just gets smaller); leftover eaters feed the mushrooms, which help the plants; magic eaters need nothing; a group with no food packs up and moves away (🧳, grayed) and comes back when food returns. The Field Notebook shows Balanced, Wobbly or Falling apart with one plain sentence, a star when the guess matched, and every group's before and after with the reason. The Food web shows sun and plants, plant eaters, meat eaters, leftover eaters with mushrooms, and magic eaters; tapping anything asks What if it moved away? and colors who would get hungry or grow. Seasons, plants and groups save per student. **Creature Maker (Build Queue 98, shipped 2026-10-13; her words: "claudia, build the creature maker next. keep the queue going for all Supernature development"):** Frankenstein hosts. Eight steps with Back, Next and step dots: Start (build from scratch, remix a found creature marked remix ok, a Spark surprise, or explore real ones in the Encyclopedia), Body (six body plans: four legs, two legs, flier, swimmer, slitherer, floater; head; 1 to 3 eyes), Parts (legs, arms or fins by body plan; tail; wings; horns), Look (fur, scales, feathers, shell or slime; two colors from 14), Mind (personality, pack or alone, smarts 1 to 5, diet including moonlight and dreams, size, usual energy on her 5 faces), Home (land and a place on the Globe, frontiers included), Name (a science name from word part tiles its traits suggest, with cera, derm, pter and saur added to the parts; a friendly name; writing the name with the wand; one sentence that must start with a capital letter and end with punctuation; a fun fact), and Page (a preview, then Save). Every option shows a picture of the creature with that change. The creature is drawn live in the same pixel style as the Encyclopedia art (a TypeScript port of the art kit, `src/lib/supernatureMaker.ts`), and its body traits, the lands it likes and how it moves all come from its parts. Undo and Redo for every change. Saved creatures (up to 12) get a page in a new tenth chapter, My Creatures, with Change it and Remove, and move into the Habitat with their own hearts and energy. Not checked on an iPad yet. **Encyclopedia, Habitat and Home round (2026-10-13, her words, verbatim, in order):** (1) "the art for the creatures is hard to find. based on the attatched, lets make the following pixel art assets in 2d photo, not worrying about making them move right now. lets have them categorized in the book. have a table of contents that is functional that students can use to navitate within their encyclepidia of monseters: for example, egyptian gods & goddesses (greek, egyptian, and roman priority), creatures (cerberus, cyclops, ogre) sprits and demons (demons), magicla beings (unicorn, dragons, fairies, pixes, golem, troll) airborn (raven, thunderbird, siren, pegasus, phoenix), water (hydra, lraken, Loc Ness, Champ (monter of lake champlain must be included), hybrids (sphinx, centraur, chimera), shapshifters and triksters (werewolf), colossal creatures (yeti, igfood)" (with a Myth Creatures Box picture, the Craftpix RPG monster pack and a Greek gods pack); (2) "make sure the encylepidas have both facts (like origin) but also a narrative story about the creature"; (3) "Imrove general function and navigation of the super nature Home Screen. Make sure door and bookshelf and fireplace, and vending machine are placed on the line where the floor meets the wall. Remove mushrooms from indoors. Place globe on a table. Enclipedia should be accessed by clicking book shelf."; (4) "remove word part ook for now"; (5) "ensure book has clear back button and all features can easily go ack to main home screen in sueprnature by clicking a home icon in the top right corner beside sounds."; (6) "improve general features of encclepida, clauida. make sure tabs are navigatable. simple designs showing the types of creatures. text should be properly aligned."; (7) "only found creatures should be placed in habitat outside"; (8) "habitat view needs to be improved. right column is unessaruly open at all times. bottom icons are difficult to understand purpose."; (9) "give features for game similar to Spores video game and biomes physical board game to allow for more habitat interactions.natrual disasters, day/night, weather, etc. are all part of habitats and should be playable. potions can be created to heal creatures that have been damaged by weather or totherwise. allow for more "God" sandbox controls as well as unpredictable effects. only happen when viewing in habitat screen" (with four packs: VFX 2D, Storm Wind 3D, Weather & Nature SFX, Weather Overlays); (10) "lets use this frankenstein for the creature builder" (a picture with no file); (11) "use otehr pixel tesutres ive uploaded to improve the habitat view"; (12) "dont call the controls "God controls" or anything, just allow for control". **Done (all shipped 2026-10-13):** **Encyclopedia:** 51 creatures in 9 chapters (Gods and Goddesses with Greek, Egyptian and Roman groups; Creatures; Spirits and Demons; Magical Beings; Airborne; Water, with Champ; Hybrids; Shapeshifters and Tricksters; Colossal Creatures). Every creature has pixel art (Zeus, Athena, Poseidon, Medusa, the Demon, the Jinn and the Dragon from her packs; the other 44 drawn in code in the same chibi style, generator in `scripts/supernature-art/`), a Facts side (origin, where it lives, size, power, energy face, traits, word history) and a Story side (a short narrative that reads itself aloud, with a Read to me switch). A working table of contents (Greek, Egyptian and Roman jump straight to their gods), chapter ribbons down the right edge that work from anywhere, a 12-slot grid per chapter with silhouettes for creatures not found yet, Previous and Next at the bottom, swipe to flip, and Back that always goes up one level (page to Contents, Contents to Home). Text is laid out in fixed columns on the blank book pages (the tabs and ribbons printed in her book art were removed so nothing fake looks tappable). 120. ~~🍂 **Supernature Habitat: four real seasons on a shared clock, survival, baby seasons and leveling up**~~ SHIPPED 2026-10-13 (her words, 2026-10-13, verbatim): "in habitat, do four seasons (creatures must react to summer, winter, spring, fall) fall leaves should show only on fall. seasons should run automatically and be synced on devices. each season take 10 minutes. a day lasts 1 minutes (similar sun passing the sky motion to what is in the farm grow game). a night lasts 1 minutes. a season consists of 5 days (and five nights). creatures should have a breeding/spawning period if noted and otherwise can breed whenever. (keep super G rated) to level up, creatures must exsist for all four seasons and survive. their biomarkers should be effected by all natural disasters and seasons. creatures can perish/die if they do not survive the elements. their adaptations and potions can help them through hard times. make sure all animations and effects are corresponded to seasons, wether, etc." **Clock:** every device works the season out from the real time (`seasonClock` in `src/lib/supernatureSeasons.ts`): 1 minute of day, 1 minute of night, 5 days and 5 nights make a 10 minute season, Spring, Summer, Fall, Winter, so a student's devices always agree. The HUD shows the season, Day N of 5, day or night, a season strip and the time left. **Sun:** the sun (and the moon at night) arcs from the left edge of the land to the right like the Farm's sun; the sky is brightest at noon, warmer at sunrise and sunset, and each season has its own sky color. **Reactions (`supernatureAdapt.ts`):** winter is cold for bodies with no thick fur (desert and scaly creatures get chilly; fur stays cozy, swimmers swim under the ice, fire creatures stay toasty); summer is hot for thick fur (desert bodies bask, swimmers cool off); spring is nesting and spawning time; in fall fliers get ready, fur grows a winter coat and plant eaters gather nuts. Hard seasons cost one heart every 30 seconds without help; the shelter, adaptations and potions protect. **Survival:** at the end of a season, a creature with 0 hearts did not survive: it fades away gently like stardust (never shown hurt), its family comes back the next spring at level 1, or right away with a Redux potion. **Leveling:** a creature levels up after living through all four seasons (the creature card shows which seasons it has); this replaced the old balanced season rule. **Babies:** water creatures spawn in spring and fliers nest in spring (2 babies when fed), snow creatures have babies in snug winter dens (like polar bears), everyone else any season; the creature card says which. **Biomarkers:** hearts, status and energy change with seasons (cold bodies slow down in winter, spring parents are busy) as well as disasters. **Animations and effects:** falling leaves only in fall (wind no longer shows leaves in other seasons), leaf piles and orange trees in fall, snow cover, light snowfall, paler trees and an icy pond in winter, blossoms and drifting petals in spring, brighter colors and a bigger sun in summer; fireflies only on spring and summer nights; no birdsong in winter (wind instead), frogs only in spring and summer; in winter rain falls as snow and in summer snow falls as rain; surprise weather and disasters fit the season (blizzards in winter, wildfires and droughts in summer, floods in spring). **Seasons while away:** they are worked out on return (up to 8): everyone waited in the shelter, so only creatures already asleep at 0 hearts do not make it; a Field Notebook shows what happened. **Guessing:** Next season became 🔮 Guess the season: the guess is saved and checked by the Field Notebook when the season ends on its own. Not checked live yet, including the ten minute season change.

A picture of Azalea should appear and it should walk students through. i want it to be an ABA style conversation where students are walking through. allow them to use their voice to talk with azalea. have her help walk through the specifics. claudia how can we improve this feature". Her picture is saved as `public/characters/azalea.png` (white background removed) with a head crop for the corner button (`azalea-head.png`). `src/components/GameReportBubble.tsx` rebuilt: the corner Report button shows Azalea; tapping it opens Azalea, who slides in and bobs beside a speech bubble. **ABA style:** one question at a time; every question read aloud by Azalea (human voice, Bright and Friendly); picture choices; behavior-specific praise before each next question; paw prints show how many steps are left; prompt fading (after 14 seconds the first choice pulses and Azalea says how to answer, after 34 seconds "Take your time. I am right here."); "I am not sure" is always allowed; Back on every step; a review of the whole report read back before sending; big praise at the end ("You are a real bug detective"). **Bug path:** what kind of problem (screen looks wrong, a button does not work, froze or stuck, sound or voice, money or rewards, something else), what you were doing, what happened (talk, voice memo or type; required), one time or again and again, can you still play. **Idea path:** what kind of idea (new thing, how it looks, easier, harder, sounds or music, something else), the idea (required), why it would be better. **Voice:** 🎤 Talk to Azalea answers by speaking: on picture questions her words are matched to a choice (for example "it froze" picks It froze or got stuck), and on open questions they are written into the box. **Voice memo:** 🎙️ Record a voice memo (up to 60 seconds), play it back, record again or delete; it uploads with the report (Supabase videos bucket, `voice-memos/` folder) and the teacher's Review Inbox shows a player for it. Each report also records the device, screen size and time automatically. **Every game:** all native games, Quiz Mode, the Gym, Science Lab, Supernature, plus Farmers Market and Grammar Sandbox (new). Grammar Gus is still left out because nothing may overlap his machine (see the ideas below). Not checked live on an iPad yet, including the microphone permission and whether the videos bucket accepts the memo files (if it does not, the report still sends and says the memo could not be saved).
    - **Claudia's ideas to make it better (her question "claudia how can we improve this feature"; waiting on her pick):** (1) close the loop: when the teacher marks a report fixed, Azalea tells the student next time ("Your teacher fixed the bug you found!") and gives a 🔍 Bug Detective sticker; (2) a snapshot of the screen attached automatically, so the student does not have to describe what it looked like; (3) the game passes in what was happening (level, last question, last button) so the report is exact; (4) Azalea inside Grammar Gus's Menu, so Gus gets reporting without anything over his machine; (5) a teacher setting for how much help Azalea gives (more pictures and modeling for some students, fewer steps for others), matching each student's prompting level; (6) a small reward for a complete, clear report, approved by the teacher so it cannot be farmed; (7) a "show me" step where the student taps the spot on a frozen picture of the game where the problem was.

Reports where the student cannot play get a red edge. Filters: every game or one game, All / Bugs / Ideas, Open only; ⬇️ Download CSV of what is shown. **Clear steps:** right after bug or idea, Azalea asks "Is it about (this game)?" with the game's picture, "A different game" (then every game's picture to tap) or "Not a game: the app, Town Square or my money", then "Which part of it?" The report is filed under the game the student picked. **Explicit support for communication needs:** one question at a time, every question and choice read aloud, a model sentence and sentence starters on every open question, the picked answer said back, the transcript of what they said shown and read back, prompts after waiting, "I am not sure" always allowed, and a full read-back before sending.

It needs safety: a place to hide or a way to escape."), read aloud with Listen: scared when hunted, frightened in a disaster that hurts its body, uncomfortable when too cold or hot, frustrated when hungry, lonely when a pack creature is alone, sad when homesick, tired when low on hearts, exhausted at 0 hearts, sleepy when hibernating, shaky but proud after escaping, proud after learning a skill, calm or content when safe. **Taking creatures in and out:** 🧺 Take out of the Habitat on a creature's card, and a 🧺 Creatures tile in the bottom bar listing the ones not in play. Both open a confirmation (read aloud with Listen) that says it will (or will no longer) be in play, its levels and learned skills start over from zero (level 0 with its 3 starting skills), and exactly how the food web in that biome changes (who could be hunted, who has more or less food, plants). Anubis weighs a feather on his golden scale, guards the shelter and guides lost creatures home at night (healing one); Zeus throws a tiny thunderbolt (a flash); Poseidon makes a wave; Athena shares wise advice (heals) and plants an olive seed (a plant grows faster); a unicorn, Isis, the phoenix, the siren and a jinn heal a friend; fairies, pixies, Curupira, Mars and the long dragon help plants grow; Golem sinks into the ground with earth magic; the kraken hides in ink; Nessie and Champ peek out and dive; the werewolf howls at the full moon (night only). Made creatures act from their bodies. **Fauna:** six wild critters (leaf bug, firebug, stag beetle, scorpion, sea star, night butterfly) appear in the biomes where they really live; tapping one "spots" it (watch, do not touch) and adds it to the book.
136. ~~🌱 **Supernature: plants with plant lore (naturopathy and alchemy), planting and harvesting by biome, wild flora to collect**~~ SHIPPED 2026-10-14 (her words, 2026-10-14, verbatim): "plants should have a level of naturopathy/alchemy. plants can be used in potion making. some plants should be bad for you and have negative effects, and some should be healing. plants can be planted and harvested within biomes (relative to their actual survival: coral in water, for example). flora/fauna exsisits naturalal in biomes too and should be planted sparcely and randoml,y to be collected." **Plants (`src/lib/supernaturePlants.ts`, pixel art `scripts/supernature-art/plants.py`):** 23 plants, each living only where it really could, with a real plant-lore fact and an alchemy use: healing (chamomile, lavender, peppermint, coneflower, willow bark, water lily, snow lotus, aloe), food (clover, fern, cattail, arctic moss, prickly pear, sagebrush, kelp, coral), magic (glowcap mushroom) and harmful (sneezeweed, foxglove, sundew, stinging nettle, sea anemone, and the snapjaw flower from her Plants pack). Coral, kelp and anemones only live in the Ocean; arctic moss and snow lotus are the only ones that grow in winter. **Wild plants and critters** are scattered sparsely and randomly in each biome, new every season (3 or 4 plants and usually one critter, sparkling so they can be found); tapping a plant picks it into the pantry as a Cauldron ingredient (harmful ones are "picked with gloves" just to learn about, never ingredients) and opens a discovery card (kind, lore, alchemy, where it grows, Listen). **Garden:** four garden spots in every biome; tap an empty one to plant anything already found that could really grow there (with the reason when it cannot: "Coral only lives in the ocean.", "It is winter"); it sprouts in 1 minute and is ready in 3 (it keeps growing while away), using the growing sprites from her pack; harvesting gives 2 for the pantry. **Creatures and plants:** plant eaters nibble wild plants: healing plants give back hearts, food plants one heart, harmful ones cause a G-rated trouble (sneezing, a tummy ache, sticky, itchy, stung, startled by a snapjaw) that shows in their feelings as uncomfortable (Yellow Zone). **Plant potions:** Herba (aloe + willow bark: 2 hearts and no plant troubles), Calma (chamomile + lavender + water lily: Green Zone calm for the season), Germina (clover + fern: every garden plant here ready now), Antidota (peppermint + coneflower: cures and blocks harmful plants for the season); the Cauldron lists Habitat plants separately ("find or grow them") and the Shop does not sell them. **Plant lore level:** 🌿 Plant and Critter Book on the right side shows every plant and critter (silhouettes until found) and the student's plant lore rank: Seed, Sprout, Herbalist, Alchemist, Master Alchemist.

One magic screen titled Cauldron, night sky and gold pixel theme. **Left shelf:** ⚗️ Elements (24 real elements and kitchen chemicals as pixel art, each with a mythic nickname and a real fact, e.g. Helium "Featherlight") and 🌿 Magic (the pantry's ingredients); drag into the pot or tap; swiping up and down scrolls the shelf. **Middle:** the pot with chips you tap to take out, Heat, Stir (button or draw a circle on the pot), Chill and Zap, each with its own effect (flames, frost, lightning, a twister), 🪄 Brew and 🧹 Empty. **Right, the Grimoire:** 28 recipe cards rebuilt on real science (Aero needs Helium, Aqua is Hydrogen + Oxygen + a Zap, Fort is Iron + Carbon heated into steel, Pyro is Carbon + Oxygen + Heat), each with its myth (Hermes, Poseidon, Hephaestus, Prometheus), a clue, the key element, helpers, the spark of magic and the action; what you still need glows on the shelf. Secret cards stay locked with a clue riddle, and can also be discovered in a free experiment. **Results:** no key element, or no magic in a free experiment, is a pixel puff of smoke; too much in the pot, an unrelated extra, baking soda + vinegar, or sodium + water bubbles over (foam spills over the rim and drips); nothing is used up on a fail. Every potion pops out in its own fun-shaped bottle (round, heart, star, tall, diamond, gourd) and is only bottled after the student writes its spell name. **Free experiment:** a match discovers that recipe; anything new with a real element and magic opens **My recipe card**: name with a capital letter, a purpose (prefilled when the elements point to one, required otherwise), an optional sentence with Say it first, the required spell name trace, and an optional **Trace the whole card** (name, purpose, every ingredient, the action, one word at a time). Saved cards live in the Grimoire's ⚡ My potions tab and can be brewed again; each makes 1 bottle of the matching Cookbook potion (Flying makes Aero) so it works in the Habitat. **Power ups:** any brewed potion or card can be powered up with 10 questions from her question sets per level, 3 levels (✨ Charged, ✨✨ Mighty, ✨✨✨ Legendary), saved per student. The old Recipes and Mixing Lab tabs and the science essence are gone (the Science Lab is entirely separate). **Not yet wired:** power levels show on the cards and bottles but do not yet change how strong a potion is in the Habitat or battles; Weak and Strong change only the number of bottles.

234. 🎡 **Build the Feelings Wheel into the login check-in, with zone colors, independent rings and an energy step** SHIPPED 2026-10-20 (her words, verbatim, answering item 233's mock-up): "use inside out fearful, add zone color based on wheel ring. no yellow boarder around each word unless it would be in zone yellow. after feelng is shown, hva the student select from their energy level (same as biome/habitat). build it. make sure smooth animations, simple sound effects (ticky when spinning, small notifying sound on selection. simple sound when it adds the second ring to the wheel). make sure each outer ring can be spun independently without spinning the inner rings. claudia, you can do this"
   - **What shipped:** the login check-in now opens on the Feelings Wheel (`src/components/FeelingsWheel.tsx`, words, zones and colors in `src/lib/feelingsWheel.ts`) instead of the four zone buttons. Half a prize wheel at the bottom of the screen; drag or flick a ring to spin it, tap a slice to turn it to the pointer. It starts with the seven center feelings. When a ring stops, the slice's picture opens out of its pie shape into a square card (word read aloud, its zone chip, "This is how I feel", "See more like this" with a little pie of the next feelings). Staying 5 seconds (countdown shown) or tapping See more grows the next ring outside it, up to three rings. **Rings spin on their own:** spinning the outside ring leaves the inner rings still; spinning an inner ring folds away the rings outside it (they belonged to the old feeling) and opens that ring's new feeling. The slice under the pointer on each inner ring stays outlined as the path. Back removes the outside ring.
   - **Zone colors (her words: "add zone color based on wheel ring. no yellow boarder around each word unless it would be in zone yellow"):** every word's tag is its own zone color (blue, green, yellow or red) on every ring, and the zone of the word she picks is the check-in's zone, so the zone tools, the Neighbor re-check timing and her reports work as before. Claudia's zones: Happy and most of its words Green (Playful, Cheeky, Sensitive Yellow); Surprised and its words Yellow (Shocked Red, Awe Green); Bad Blue (Busy, Pressured, Rushed, Stressed, Overwhelmed, Unfocused Yellow, Out of control Red); Fearful Yellow (Weak, Rejected, Helpless, Inadequate, Inferior, Worthless, Insignificant, Excluded Blue; Threatened, Frightened, Distraught Red); Angry Red (Let down, Distant, Withdrawn, Numb Blue; Humiliated, Bitter, Frustrated, Critical and their milder words Yellow); Disgusted Yellow (Awful, Nauseated Blue; Horrified Red); Sad and all its words Blue (Embarrassed Yellow). She can ask for any word to change zone.
   - **Energy step (her words: "after feelng is shown, hva the student select from their energy level (same as biome/habitat)"):** after "This is how I feel", the student sees their picture, "You feel ___." with its zone and picks Very high, High, Just right, Low or Very low with the same five faces as the Supernature Habitat (Change my feeling goes back). Then Green finishes and the other zones open the support menu as before. The energy is saved on the check-in with no new SQL (stored as "Furious | high energy" in the feeling word column and split back apart when read) and shows in the check-in log, its printout and the Review Inbox.

273. ✍️ **Typed answers: three support levels that move with the student, per-box right marks, hints from Help** SHIPPED 2026-10-20 (symbol sentence answers) (her answer 3 above, verbatim): "if we have levels of support for the typed answers we could say level 1: no support, level 2: spell check says if its wrong but doesnt corrrect. only says if it is or isnt part of the grammar. level 3: full spell check and correction list option, yes voice type. yes move help ladder based on responses. level of support should fluxiate based on student repsonses and whetehr they are right or wrong. each typed field can be marked as correct if answered, but dont mark the whole thing as right until all are correct. student in help button can ask for hints if consistently incorrect" **What shipped:** `src/lib/typedSupport.ts` keeps each student's help level in a `typedsupport:<id>` style row: everyone starts at level 2; 3 sentences right on the first try in a row means one level less help, 2 missed in a row means one level more. The symbol sentence answer (`SymbolSentenceAnswer.tsx`) shows the level as a small pill and follows it: **Level 1 (on my own):** no spell check, no reasons, each box is just marked right or "Not quite. Try again." **Level 2 (word checks):** says why a box is wrong (for example "That's not a verb") and says "Check the spelling of this word" once for a word it does not know, without fixing it (keeping the same word the second time is accepted). **Level 3 (full help):** the iPad spell check and autocorrect turn on, a list of close spellings of the right kind appears under a box to tap (`suggestWords`), and a 🎤 on each box types a spoken word. **Every level:** each box that is right gets a green ✓ and locks; the sentence counts only once every box is right (first try counts as right for scores). After 2 misses a 💡 Help button gives a hint per box still wrong (what kind of word it needs, its meaning and three example words of that kind; any fitting word counts, so this never gives the answer away). The set's own Spell check setting is now decided by the level; the dice and grammar check settings still apply. **Not yet:** Mad Lib answers keep their own hint setting (her message was about the symbol sentence typed answers).

285. 🔑 **Vercel steps for the voices key, once more** ANSWERED 2026-10-20 (her words, verbatim): "give me vercel steps here agin" Answered in chat in 8 steps.

   - **The one screen (replaces the Recipes and Mixing Lab tabs):** left, the Element Shelf: the same real elements and substances as the Science Lab (H, He, C, N, O, Na, Mg, Al, Cl, K, Ca, Fe, Cu, Li and the kitchen chemicals), as pixel vials grouped by family color, with a ✨ Table button that opens the real periodic table; plus a small Magic shelf (fairy wing, dew, Habitat plants, shop ingredients). Center, one big Cauldron with four action tools around it: 🔥 Heat, 🌀 Stir (draw circles), ❄️ Chill, ⚡ Zap. Right, the Grimoire page: the potion goal card (or "Free experiment"), the science clue, and the potion book.
   - **Potion = real science base + a spark of magic + an action.** Each potion keeps its name and job but gets a recipe rooted in what the element really does: Aero (flying) needs Helium, lighter than air; Thermo (warm) needs Iron + Oxygen + salt, like a real hand warmer; Cryo (cold) needs Nitrogen, the super cold gas; Aqua needs Hydrogen + Oxygen + ⚡ Zap, which really makes water; Pyro needs Carbon + Oxygen + 🔥 Heat (burning); Fort (tough) needs Iron + Carbon (steel); Lumin (light) needs Magnesium, which burns bright white; Vita (healing) needs Calcium (bones) + a healing plant; Mega (giant) needs yeast + sugar (bread rises); Velo (speed) needs Lithium (battery power); Sicco (dry) needs salt (pulls water out); Ancora (heavy) needs Iron; Pneumo (breath) needs Oxygen. The magic ingredient makes it a potion instead of a chemistry experiment.
   - **Not the same as the Science Lab:** one cauldron instead of three beakers; goals and silly outcomes instead of a sandbox; actions (heat, stir, chill, zap) instead of only pouring; smoke and color stories instead of lab equipment. The chemistry engine underneath is shared, so real reactions still happen for real reasons.
   - **Animations:** a colored poof of smoke for every addition, smoke that changes color with the brew, flames under the pot for Heat, frost creeping up the sides for Chill, a lightning crackle for Zap, faster bubbles while stirring, a cartoon BOOM with the pot hopping (no harm, ever), a bottle that fills and corks itself, and silly "near misses" (the cauldron hiccups, burps a frog-shaped cloud, sneezes glitter).
   - **Help that fades:** each goal card has a science clue riddle ("To fly, you need something lighter than air."); a 2nd hint glows the right element family on the table; a 3rd glows the exact element. A wrong mix tells what it did ("The helium lifted it a little, but it needs something to hold it together.").
   - **Plan for the build (after her answers):** 1 the combined screen with the shelf, cauldron, actions and Grimoire; 2 the 28 potions rewritten as science recipes, with clues and hints; 3 the animations and silly outcomes; 4 the free experiment mode on the shared chemistry; 5 her answers to the questions below.
   - **Her 10 questions** (my suggestion after each): 1. One screen with two ways to play, a goal card or free experiment? (yes) 2. How exact is a recipe: the key element is required and extras are flexible, or exact only? (key element required, near misses still make a weaker potion) 3. How hard to start: 1 element + 1 magic, building up to 3 elements + an action? (yes) 4. Keep the 28 potion names and jobs, with new science recipes, and keep the potions students already own? (yes) 5. Elements free once learned, magic ingredients still from the Shop and Habitat? (yes) 6. How silly should failures be? (funny and never punishing: hiccups, frog clouds, glitter) 7. How are elements unlocked: shared with Science Lab learning, by brewing, or all open? (shared, plus brewing unlocks) 8. Should questions be part of it (answer to get a clue, or to power up a potion)? (a right answer powers up a potion to double strength; clues stay free) 9. Keep the "write the spell" tracing at the end? (yes, as the potion's name) 10. How much real science to read: one sentence plus read-aloud, with a "Why it works" card after each potion? (yes)

- 2026-10-12: 🗣️ Human voices (item 93). **Real human voices:** a new voice service (`api/tts.ts`, OpenAI gpt-4o-mini-tts) reads every line in a natural neural voice, each character with its own human voice and speaking style: the reader voice for questions and stories (warm, calm teacher), Doc Fishing (slow, deep Southern drawl), Grammar Gus (prim British), the Neighbors' and Townspeople's voice presets (deep, warm, calm, crisp, upbeat, bright, cheerful, playful, country), and pets (a small happy voice). Every line is cached for a year by Vercel, so a line read again costs nothing; new lines cost about 1.5 cents per minute of speech. It switches on by itself once `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set in the Vercel project (until then the app checks `/api/tts?probe=1`, gets "not set up", and uses the device). Only this app can use it. Anything that stops speech also stops a human voice. **Better device voices meanwhile (and as the backup):** read-aloud always picks the most human voice on the device (Premium, then Enhanced or Natural voices), never the novelty robot voices (Fred, Zarvox, Bells and the like, also removed from the student voice picker), and characters no longer get big pitch shifts (what made them sound robotic); pets no longer use the squeaky high pitch. Not changed: the Library's immersive reader (it already picks the best voice and needs word-by-word timing that only device voices give). CLAUDE.md has the new standing rule.

## ✍️ SYMBOL SENTENCE WRITER: typed-answer question sets (Build Queue 166 and 218), full development spec

Her words: 166 (2026-10-14) "lets make a new feature for question sets where students will have to have a text input. my goal is that students will be scaffolded, starting with filling in one word of a setnence, and working their way up to having full sentences created by them. we are going to use my symbol sentences. lets fully develop this before you build it at all"; 218 (2026-10-15) "tell me what you think im asking for question sets with typed answers, and lets build that out in development plan while you work". **Status: DESIGNED, NOT BUILT.** Nothing is built until she OKs this spec (or changes it). Design PDF: `docs/symbol-sentence-writer-design.pdf`.

### What she is asking for (in plain words)
1. A new kind of question set where students **type** the answer instead of tapping a choice.
2. It is built on **her symbol sentences**: the sentence cards where every word sits under its grammar symbol (pointing hand noun, crown proper noun, magnet article, arrows verb, pencil circle adjective, gear adverb, box preposition, double arrow conjunction, cycle pronoun, ! interjection).
3. It **grows with the student**: it starts tiny (type one missing word in a sentence, with help) and step by step works up to the student writing a whole sentence of their own that matches the symbols.
4. It is fully planned first. No code until she approves.

### What already exists to build on
- **The sentences:** `src/lib/symbolSentences.ts` (her deck, each word tagged with its word class) plus her 10 new proper noun sentences (34 to 43) from `Grammar_Sentences_Comprehensive.zip`, and her new symbol icons (already cut for the Literacy Manipulatives whiteboard, item 175).
- **Typed answers:** question sets already have a `fill` type (`FillBlankQuestion`: prompt, answer, optional word bank) and a typo-tolerant checker (`isCloseEnoughAnswer` in `src/lib/answerMatch.ts`, short words need exact spelling).
- **Where questions run:** Assignments (`QuizTask`), Quiz Mode, and the game question screen. The one-try rule (item 209) and the 95% focus rule (item 210) apply.

### The two ladders (move separately)
**A. Help ladder, 8 levels** (what the student types):
1. One missing word, with two word cards to choose from to copy (errorless start).
2. One missing word, on their own.
3. Two missing words.
4. Every naming, action and describing word missing (the small words stay).
5. Look, cover, write: see the whole sentence, it hides, type it all; checks for a capital letter at the start and punctuation at the end.
6. Write the whole sentence from the symbols alone, with word helpers to tap.
7. My own sentence that matches the symbols; each typed word lights up under its symbol as it fits (noun under the hand, verb under the arrows...).
8. My own sentence, then I pick the symbols for it.

**B. Sentence path:** her sentences 1 to 43, simple to harder (the deck's own order), plus any she adds.

**Moving up and down:** up a level after 4 of the last 5 are right on the first try; after 3 misses in a row a step down is offered (never forced). Errorless help: second try shows the first letter, third try shows the answer to copy (counts as effort, not right). The one-try lock (item 209) applies to money and points only: the student still finishes the word with help so they always leave with the right sentence.

### The student screen (iPad first)
- The symbol row on top, the sentence with blank boxes under each symbol, the keyboard below; the boxes stay in the top half so the iPad keyboard never covers them.
- iPad auto-capitalize, autocorrect and spell check are **off** (spelling, capital letters and punctuation are the skill).
- The Next key on the keyboard moves to the next box; 🔊 on every symbol, every word and the whole sentence (human voice).
- Right: the word slides into place under its symbol with a chime; the finished sentence is read aloud.

### The teacher side
- A new question set type "✍️ Symbol Sentence Writer" in Question Sets, preloaded with her 43 sentences.
- Pick which sentences and which levels; set each student's starting level, see their highest level, and lock a level if she wants.
- Add her own sentences: type the sentence, the app suggests the symbols, she fixes any.
- Question Reports show exactly what was typed (and the help used); a ladder picture per student; a wall of the sentences each student wrote at levels 7 and 8.

### Build plan (after her OK)
- **Phase 1:** the data (sentences with symbols, levels), the student screen for levels 1 to 4, typed-answer checking, Assignments and Quiz Mode, Question Reports.
- **Phase 2:** levels 5 and 6 (look cover write, capital letter and punctuation checks), the teacher controls (start, highest, lock), her own sentences with suggested symbols.
- **Phase 3:** levels 7 and 8 (her own sentences matched to symbols), the student wall, game pop-ups (levels 1 to 3 only).

### Her 10 questions (my suggestion in brackets; her answer decides)
1. Use the new icons here, and switch the Grammar Sandbox and Gus to them too? (Yes here; the Sandbox and Gus later, her call.)
2. In a blank, only the card's own word counts, or any word that fits? (Only the card's word at levels 1 to 4; any fitting word at 7 and 8.)
3. Spelling: exact, or close spellings count? (Exact for short words, one typo allowed for long ones, the same as today's typed answers; the right spelling is always shown.)
4. Show up inside games too? (Only levels 1 to 3, as pop-ups.)
5. Allow voice typing (the iPad microphone)? (No; typing is the skill. A setting she can turn on per student.)
6. The up and down rule above (4 of 5 up, a step down offered after 3 misses)? (Yes.)
7. Students' own sentences (levels 7 and 8): checked by the app, and shown on her wall? (The app checks that the words fit the symbols; she sees every one on the wall.)
8. Sentence order: her deck's order, or mixed? (Her order.)
9. Rewards: $1 like other questions, with whole-sentence levels (5 to 8) counting double? (Yes.)
10. The name: "Symbol Sentence Writer"? (Or her choice.)

### The SQL details

**2026-10-01, production outage, hotfixed in code but not fully resolved:** saving any activity/question set started failing ("Could not find the 'student_description' column of 'activity_library' in the schema cache") because `supabase/schema.sql` already has `student_title`/`student_description` columns defined for the `activity_library` table (`alter table activity_library add column if not exists ...`), but that migration was never actually run against the live Supabase database — this sandbox has no Supabase credentials/CLI, so a schema.sql edit is local-only and never auto-applies to production. The code was hotfixed to stop sending those two fields so saving works again right now, but that means **a student's own title/description typed into an activity is silently not being saved** until this is fixed for real.

**What she needs to do, in the Supabase SQL Editor (already open in her browser per the screenshot that caught this):**
```sql
alter table activity_library add column if not exists student_title text;
alter table activity_library add column if not exists student_description text;
```
Once that's run, tell the next session (or this one) so the two fields can be added back to the save payload in `src/lib/sync.ts`'s `activityToRow`. This is the same class of bug flagged earlier this session as a standing lesson — a schema.sql migration being written doesn't mean it ran — and it's worth a one-time check of the rest of schema.sql's `alter table` statements against the live database for any other silently-unapplied columns, rather than waiting for each one to surface as its own outage.

**Also pending (2026-10-01 and 2026-10-04), same SQL Editor, both safe to run any time; until then the app works but these don't save to the database:**
- `chess_games` (Slime Chess personal leaderboard): the full `create table if not exists chess_games ...` block plus its policies (given in chat 2026-10-01; also in `supabase/schema.sql`).
- `style_looks` (Style: saved looks; the teacher's look also saves on her device meanwhile):
```sql
create table if not exists style_looks (
  owner_id text primary key,
  look jsonb not null default '{}',
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
alter table style_looks enable row level security;
drop policy if exists style_looks_select on style_looks;
create policy style_looks_select on style_looks for select to anon, authenticated using (true);
drop policy if exists style_looks_insert on style_looks;
create policy style_looks_insert on style_looks for insert to anon, authenticated with check (true);
drop policy if exists style_looks_update on style_looks;
create policy style_looks_update on style_looks for update to anon, authenticated using (true) with check (true);
drop policy if exists style_looks_delete on style_looks;
create policy style_looks_delete on style_looks for delete to authenticated using (true);
```

## PART A — Shipped Features (the platform as it exists today)

Organized into four groups per direct teacher instruction: **Game & Play**, **Educational/Academic**, **ABA/SEL/Behavioral**, and **Platform/Other**. Every individual feature gets its own entry: what it is, exactly how a student or teacher interacts with it, and why it exists. A feature that touches more than one group (pets, for example, are a play feature whose training system is also a real ABA design) is written up in full once, under whichever group is its primary purpose, and cross-referenced by name from the other group rather than repeated.

### GROUP 1: GAME & PLAY FEATURES

#### A1. The 3D World: Town Square

The open-air hub every student lands in after login (not a 2D task list first, by direct teacher instruction after reviewing an earlier version). A student walks their avatar around using a repositionable on-screen D-pad, keyboard arrows, or click/tap-to-walk with a hover-preview marker showing exactly where they'll land. The camera follows behind and above the avatar; a student can drag to look around, use explicit look buttons, and tilt the camera vertically, with movement speed adjustable per student (0.5x to 2x) in Settings. Every wandering character (Player, Neighbors, ambient Townspeople) is scaled to read as a real person (Kenney Mini Character models brought up to human height after an early version had everyone looking like ants on the lawn).

Every building in the square (Bank, Store, Post Office, Welcome Center, Computer Desk, Home, Pet Shelter, Island Dock, Cinema, Arcade, or a teacher-custom role/external link) can be walked up to and opened with a one-tap Confirm card; a "Closed/Coming Soon" role exists so an unfinished building reads as intentional, not broken. Collision is real: buildings block movement using their actual rotated footprint (not a generic circle), so a student can never clip through a wall. A Map view shows an overhead grid with double-click-to-teleport or double-click-to-open-a-building.

Navigation/HUD: a single top-right radial pie menu holds Tasks, What now?, Help/Break, Settings/Map/My Stuff (under "More"), My Home, and Companion, all in one place per direct teacher instruction (a deliberate, teacher-approved override of the general "Help must never be gated behind a menu" rule elsewhere in the app, see Part D). Clicking the player's own avatar opens the same pie ("master menu" behavior). A "What's New" changelog book (see A39) auto-opens the first time something new ships that affects a student.

A computer desk placed in the square is the task entry point (a retro browser-styled frame opens the student's daily rotation), so "go do my schoolwork" is a real in-world action, not a separate app section. The world-object catalog enforces a hard zero-weapons rule automatically. A Wizard ThunderSword prop is the visual/interaction surface for the Tier 3 regulation lock described in A28; Help/calm-down always stays reachable through it even while it's otherwise non-dismissable.

#### A2. Home Room (Private Room)

- **2026-10-08: the student's Style character is the player here** (direct teacher instruction: "make sure new character design applies everywhere, for students (in their home)"). Same shared `StyleAvatar` as Town Square; the old player model only returns if Style is switched off for students.

Each student's own private room, picked from a catalog of real-scaled house exteriors visible on their shared "home" building in Town Square. Opens in a read-only View mode by default with a real Build Mode toggle for decorating. Walls are drawn Sims-4-style (click, drag, release) into multi-room floor plans; doors and windows snap to walls. Students paint their own walls and floors, and place furniture/yard decor from the same catalog Build Mode uses (see A4), scoped privately to their own room only. The Pet Care panel (see A5) lives here: feed/pet/play/rename/set-companion/sell, with feelings-word tags and a save-confirmation flash so an action always visibly registers.

#### A3. Creative Island

- **2026-10-08: the student's Style character is the player here** (direct teacher instruction: "make sure new character design applies everywhere, for students (in their home)"). Same shared `StyleAvatar` as Town Square; the old player model only returns if Style is switched off for students.

A Minecraft-style free-build space with the full teacher-parity object catalog, reachable by boat from Town Square's dock or directly from Home Room. Locked by default; a teacher unlocks it per student (`islandBuildUnlocked`, see A40's Student Manager). Same real collision, View mode, and custom-role support as the rest of the world. Exists specifically so building/arranging (constructionist play, the thing Minecraft Education does well) has a home that isn't scoped to the confines of one student's own room.

#### A4. Build Mode / World Editor

The placement/decorating tool underlying Town Square, Home Room, and Creative Island. Catalog: 1,000+ real 3D models across dozens of packs, each with a generated thumbnail and a real-world size class (1.0 unit = player height; see `SIZE_REFERENCE.md`). A student or teacher places an object with a ghost preview, moves it with a crosshair/D-pad, rotates it in 90-degree steps, and resizes it either with size presets (Mini through Giant) or a free-typed exact number, with a live per-object unit readout. Undo/redo is available; the teacher's shared-world changes go through a Draft to Publish/Discard cycle (so students never see a half-finished edit); a student's own room/island changes are always live. A paint brush and bucket recolor ground, sky, and asset tint, with a half-tile grid for precision. Every asset can carry a custom role (see A1), and a teacher can retint, resize, move, or delete even the game's own original fixed layout (buildings, market stalls, road tiles), not just objects placed after the tool existed.

- **Smooth movement around solid objects — SHIPPED 2026-10-11.** Her words (verbatim): "allow student players to move smothly around the edge/border of seamless objects instead of stopping them completely and having the camera view glitch because teh player. is stuck. they should instead be able to proceed smothly around the edge of the asset and continue moveing forward". **Root cause:** collision treated the player as a point and each solid object as a box grown by half a unit, and pushed the point out of each box separately, through whichever side of that box was closest. Where two objects sit edge to edge (a row of hedges, fences, stalls, buildings side by side), the point at the seam was closest to the inside ends of both boxes, so one box pushed the player back along the wall and the other pushed them forward again, every frame: the player stopped dead and the camera shook. **Fixed (collide and slide, the way most 3D games do it):** the player (and Neighbors and cars) is a round body and each object is its real rectangle; every step goes where the input says and is then pushed straight out from the nearest point of whatever it overlaps, one overlap at a time. Along a row of objects the push is always straight out from the row's face, so the player glides past every seam; corners are rounded for the body, so walking past a corner curves smoothly around it; and walking straight into something turns the step along its face toward the nearer end, keeping that direction while still blocked (no back and forth), so holding forward walks around the object and on past it. **Also:** trees are now solid only at their trunks (not the whole canopy), so students can walk between trees in the Enchanted Forest. Not checked live yet.
- **Fix: building the new town blanked Build Mode — SHIPPED 2026-10-11.** Her report (a screenshot of a blank Build Mode with the console full of errors). **Root cause:** the builder removed and added about 450 objects at once, and every one sent its own save to the cloud at the same moment. The browser ran out of connections ("net::ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES"), so saves failed and kept retrying, and then a building's 3D model could not be fetched either ("Could not load /world/models/buildings/post-office.glb: Failed to fetch"). Nothing in the 3D scene caught a failed model, so that one error took down the whole view ("WebGL context lost"). **Fixed:** (1) every save in the app now waits its turn, at most 6 at a time (`src/lib/sync.ts`), so a big change can never flood the browser again. (2) Every placed object is wrapped so a model that fails to load shows nothing and tries again a few seconds later, instead of blanking Build Mode or Town Square. (3) The builder marks itself "building" before it starts, and when it finishes it shows "Saving to the cloud: N left. Keep this page open." until every save has landed; the browser now asks before leaving a page with saves still on their way. (4) Building again never overwrites the saved old town (it is only saved when the current town is the old one). (5) If a build was cut off, the banner says "The new town did not finish building last time" with 🏗️ Finish building and ↩ Bring back the old town; the Regions panel's 🖼️ Town design section always has 🏗️ Build the new town again (clean) and ↩ Bring back the old town. Not checked live yet.

Her words (verbatim): "make sure build mode accomidates for terrain manipulation so that i can make rivers, lakes, oceans with animation (quiet water mvoement sounds) and animated fish if placed. all animals placed in build mode as a teacher should be animated when in live mode. allow terrain manipulation to be smooth, size adjustable, (research features and apply)".** Mid-build she also uploaded texture packs (wests, a 4K rock pack, 100 hand-painted textures, 5 wood textures), a 40-frame water animation (frames and mp4), and three 3D packs (rocks, tiny weeds, Yughues hand-painted plants).
  - **Research applied:** the sculpt tools in Unity Terrain, Cities: Skylines, Planet Coaster and the Sims share one model, which this follows: a height grid, soft round brushes that work while held (Raise, Lower, Smooth, Flatten), a brush size and strength, one sea level that fills any low ground with water, cliffs that turn to rock on their own, sand at the shoreline, and stroke-by-stroke undo.
  - **Build Mode:** a new **⛰️ Terrain** button on the bottom bar opens the Terrain panel: ⛰️ Raise, 🕳️ Lower, 〰️ Smooth, ▬ Flatten (to the height where the stroke began) and 💧 Water (digs below the sea level: drag a line for a river, a circle for a lake, along an edge for an ocean). **Brush size** 0.5 to 12 units ([ and ] keys), **Strength**, a **🌊 Sea level** slider (raise it to flood low ground), **↶ Undo stroke** (20 deep), **🧹 Flatten everything** (two taps), and a **🔊 Quiet water sounds** switch. Press and hold, then drag; Shift flips Raise and Lower; right-drag still turns the camera; Esc leaves the tool. A ring on the ground shows the brush size, hugging the slopes. The build grid is drawn right on the slopes. Strokes are smooth (a cosine falloff, applied every frame while held, scaled by time) and saved when the stroke ends.
  - **Ground look:** steep slopes show her rock texture (blended three ways so cliffs never stretch), shores show sand (darker, wet sand under the water), the painted ground everywhere else. Painted ground patches now bend over the hills.
  - **Water:** a moving surface over every spot below the sea level: gentle waves, sparkle and a sheen at low angles, deeper blue where it is deep, see-through where shallow, soft foam along the shore, and her 40-frame water loop flowing across it (cross-faded frame to frame). Painted 💧 Water patches move with the same loop now. Calm settings slow it.
  - **Sound:** a quiet, soft water sound made in the browser (a low flow and a gentle lapping that rises and falls) that fades in near water and out away from it, in Build Mode (around the camera's focus) and in Live mode (around the student). It starts after the first tap (the browser's rule). Very quiet by design.
  - **Living animals in Live mode:** every animal a teacher placed animates in Live mode using its own animation when it has one (fish swim, pets and farm animals idle and walk). A land animal with a walk animation strolls around its spot (within 1.8 units) and pauses, never into water; a fish swims slow loops, fully under the surface when it is in a lake; an animal with no animation of its own breathes, sways and looks around. Build Mode keeps them still for exact placing. Reduced motion keeps them in place.
  - **Everything stands on the ground:** placed objects, the placing ghost, students, Neighbors, pets, the camera and the tap markers follow the ground's height; an object's Height is measured from the ground under it. Boats float on dug water and can drive on it (it counts as water, like painted water). Walking or driving into dug water slides along the shore instead.
  - **Her texture packs:** the ground brush and the ground fill now offer her 5 wood textures, the cliff rock and boulders, and a 🎨 100 more painted textures fold with thumbnails.
  - **Her 3D packs:** converted from OBJ to GLB (73 models, with their textures, see-through leaves and normal maps) into a new 🌿 nature catalog category: 64 hand-painted plants (bushes, flowers, grass, clovers, weeds, pines, big pines), 5 tiny weeds and thistles, and a rock cluster, each sized by name (grass ankle-high, pines tree-tall) and given a catalog thumbnail.
  - **Saved as:** the `town-terrain` style_looks row (heights in centimeters, packed; no new SQL). Town Square keeps its old flat ground until she first sculpts.
  - **Checked:** a test render of a raised hill and a dug lake (rock on the hill, water, foam, grid, a fish in the lake). Not checked yet on her laptop or an iPad, or with many students.

- **Precision Build Mode: exact picking, steady dragging, exact numbers, below the ground — SHIPPED 2026-10-10. Her words (verbatim): "claudia, lets improve the build mode for me. right now, its difficult to accurately size assets, the dragging/placement and replace move arrows are buggy at best and frustrating at worst. i dont have enough accuacy for hight adjustments. i need the ability to place objects beneath the ground (lower hight so som  of it shows, but not all of the asset). i need improvements in the object layering; right now a large box surrounds the object and its difficult to move objects that have been trapped behind this box. change it so assets have boundaries ounly around the object iself, not the rectangle area around it. lets do a little research on the best highest standard for this in design games and other design programs like professionals use. fix it please and let me know when you are done. make desicisions according to accuracy, performance, and in alignment with how you believe i would direct you".**
  - **Research (the standard we matched):** Blender, Unity, Unreal and the Sims all pick an object by its real triangles (a tap that misses the shape goes through to what is behind), drag on a plane through the object with the grab point held under the cursor, start a drag only after a few pixels of movement, cancel with Esc, nudge relative to the view, and give an exact number field for every transform value (Unity's Inspector, Blender's N panel, Figma's fields). Fast triangle picking in three.js is done with a BVH index (three-mesh-bvh, already in the project through drei).
  - **Picking by the object's own shape:** the invisible padded box (130% of the footprint, full height) that every object carried is gone. Taps now hit the model's real surfaces, so an object behind another one, or between a table's legs, can be clicked directly. Each model's triangles get a BVH built once per geometry and shared by every copy, so picking stays fast. Only a really tiny model (smaller than 0.6 units) keeps a small invisible tap pad, no bigger than that minimum. This also applies to students' Home Build Mode, which shares the same renderer (`WorldObjectRenderer.tsx`).
  - **Selection shown on the object, not a box:** the wireframe box around selected and hovered objects (and around the placing ghost) is gone. A selected object glows green on its own surfaces, a hovered one glows yellow.
  - **Dragging fixed:** the drag used to follow the ground under the pointer, so the object's middle jumped to the pointer and it stopped following whenever the pointer crossed a wall or another object. It now follows an invisible plane through the object (`PlaneDragger`): the spot you grabbed stays under your finger, nothing can interrupt it, it starts only after a real 5 pixel drag (a tap never nudges anything), and Esc cancels and puts it back.
  - **Move arrows fixed:** two bugs. Holding an arrow (or −/+ and rotate) reused the position from the moment it was pressed, so a hold moved one step and stuck; the hold buttons now always use the latest value. And ↑ was fixed to north, so after turning the camera it could move things sideways or toward you; the arrows (and now the keyboard arrow keys) follow the camera, turned to the nearest side of the grid, so ↑ is always away from you. With a selection, the arrow keys move it (Shift for a tenth of a step); WASD still moves the camera.
  - **Exact numbers:** the ✥ Move panel has a **Step** choice (Grid, 0.25, 0.1, 0.01) and typed fields with −/+ for **Left/right, Front/back, Height and Turn °** (Enter or leaving the box applies, arrow keys in a box step it). A non-grid step moves exactly that distance and never snaps back to the grid.
  - **Below the ground:** height can go negative, down until only 0.05 units of the object still shows (so it can always be clicked and brought back), with the 9/0 keys, the Height field, and the placing ghost alike. The height tag under the object says "below ground" when it is sunk.
  - **Sizing:** the ⤢ Resize panel has a −/+ step choice (10%, 5%, 1%) and shows the object's real Wide · Deep · Tall in player units next to the exact size box.
  - Not checked live yet on her laptop or an iPad.

- **Stacking objects: overlap + height keys — SHIPPED 2026-10-01, direct teacher request: "in build mode, allow me to overlap build mode assets. if i press the 9 key, the object should decrease in height and if i press 0 it should raise in height so i can put objects on tables and such."** Root cause of "can't overlap": while a catalog item was armed for placing, every existing object's invisible tap box still caught the tap (and stopped the ghost from following the pointer), so nothing could ever be dropped onto a table; placed objects are now pass-through while placing (`WorldObjectRenderer`'s new `inert` prop) and catch taps normally again once placing ends. Height: **0 raises, 9 lowers** (0.1 units per press, Shift for 0.02 fine steps, never below the ground, max 20), acting on the armed ghost while placing (resets to the ground for each newly picked item) or on the selected object / multi-selection otherwise. Keyboard only, by direct teacher follow-up ("i dont want a raise/lower button thing. i just want to use keyboard controls"): the on-screen Raise/Lower buttons that briefly shipped were removed; the placing hint bar just reminds "0 raises, 9 lowers". Every move, duplicate, group rotate/resize/move, and drag now keeps an object's height instead of snapping it back to y=0, the footprint outline and toolbar float with a lifted object, and the height saves to the existing `world_objects.position` json (no migration needed). Town Square, Home Room and Island already render the saved height. Not added: the separate Island and Home Room editors still place on the ground only.
- **Selection rule + chess role fix — SHIPPED 2026-10-01, direct teacher instructions: "i only want more than one object selected if i click and hold shift while clicking the objects" and "i also cant put a chess game role assigned to the chess board."** A plain click now always selects exactly one object, even one that belongs to a group (it used to pull in every group member, which also swapped in the group toolbar that has no Name & role menu, the likely reason the Chess role couldn't be set on a grouped chess set). More than one object is selected only by Shift-clicking (Shift-click on a grouped object still adds its whole group). The ➕ Multi-select touch toggle was removed per the same instruction. Also, an object's invisible tap box no longer pokes up past the top of the model, so a table can't steal the tap from a chess set (or anything else) sitting on it. The Chess Set role itself (Name & role menu, "Chess Set (Slime Chess game)") was already present; no database change was needed.
- **Height keys follow-up + chess sets are always chess — SHIPPED 2026-10-01, teacher reports "its not raising/lowering my object" (in Town Square Build Mode) and "make sure the chess game role is able to add to the chess board too".** Reproduced in a real browser: the keys did work, but each 0.1 step was too small to see from the default camera angle (looking down from high up, a lift mostly reads as the object sliding slightly back). Steps are now 0.25 per press (Shift: 0.05), and a lifted object (or placing ghost) shows a green post down to the ground, a ground ring, and a "↕ 1.00" height tag so every press is visible. The camera-controls help panel now lists 9 / 0. Chess: any Chess Set model now gets the Slime Chess role automatically when placed, and an already-placed Chess Set with no role is treated as Slime Chess in Town Square and on Creative Island (`withDefaultRoles` in townLayout.ts); a teacher can still pick a different role for it on purpose.
- **Toolbar always in view + real overlap by dragging — SHIPPED 2026-10-01, teacher reports: "this tool bar is not working and it also needs to always be visable to the user, not in a corner, not off to the side. alwyas fully in view. also if im zoomed in the bar should be a reasonable size ... when im zoomed out it needs to also be bigger", "the toolbar buttons arnt clicking to work", and "i still cant put multiple assets in the same spot though".** Root causes: the selected-object / group / wall toolbar floated inside the 3D scene above the object (drei `Html` with distanceFactor), so it shrank when zoomed out, could slide off-screen with the object, and every tap on it also reached the 3D scene underneath (which could deselect or start other actions before the button registered). It is now a plain screen toolbar docked top-center of the Build Mode view (`ToolbarDock` in WorldEditor.tsx), rendered outside the 3D canvas: same size at every zoom level, always fully visible, popovers open straight down under it, and taps only hit the button. The old corner delete badge is gone (Delete lives on the toolbar). Overlap: objects were only pass-through while placing from the catalog; dragging a selected object onto another one was still blocked by the other object's tap box. Objects are now also pass-through mid-drag, and the release of a drag no longer counts as a "tap on empty ground" (which used to deselect the object right as you let go, so its toolbar vanished). Verified in a real browser: dragging one table onto another overlaps them, the toolbar stays up after the drag, Rotate right works from the dock, and a Chess Set placed with 0 pressed three times lands on top of the table at height 0.75 with the chess role.
- **Turn the Build Mode view from the laptop trackpad — SHIPPED 2026-10-01, direct teacher request: "i want to be able to rotate my fingers on the touchpad of my laptop to turn the view of what im seeing when im in build mode."** New `TrackpadRotate` in WorldEditor.tsx orbits the camera around the spot it's looking at (the same orbit right-drag does): a two-finger **twist** on a Mac trackpad in Safari (Safari's gesture events; Safari's pinch also zooms the scene now instead of the page), a two-finger **sideways swipe** on any trackpad in any browser (up/down still zooms), and a two-finger twist on a touch screen / iPad. The scene turns the same way the fingers move. Limitation, stated plainly: Chrome, Edge and Firefox never tell a web page about a trackpad twist (only Safari does), so in those browsers the sideways swipe is the gesture. The camera-controls help panel lists it. Not verified on a physical trackpad from this environment; if the turn direction feels backwards, flip the sign in `orbit(e.deltaX * 0.006)`.

#### A5. Pets System

A full adoptable-animal system: dogs, cats, small critters, farm animals, birds, aquatic animals, and wild animals (38 adoptable species across those categories, plus 6 held-back novelty characters; as of 2026-10-06 the whole system is paused and v2 is cats and dogs only, see Part B), each modeled at a real player-relative scale (a Great Dane reads noticeably bigger than a Chihuahua, a fish stays genuinely tiny). Every species is open to every student (no per-student scarcity) unless a future teacher tool locks one down.

**Pet Shelter** (Town Square building): every catalog pet is shown and pettable ("give a pat," a small animation) whether or not a student can afford it. A brand-new student has a one-time free-pet coupon: pick any pet, no cost, ever again. After that, pets are purchased directly with Class Cash, or pulled from the **Mystery Adoption Box** ($200, one open per real calendar day) — see A27 for its variable-ratio design. Up to 4 pets can be owned at once (`PET_OWNERSHIP_CAP`); the Shelter also offers a reward-free **Donate** option (see A35).

**Pet Journal**: a permanent, Pokédex-style log of every species a student has ever adopted, even ones later sold, filterable by category. An undiscovered species shows as a "???" silhouette. This is what makes "collect them all" mean something even though only 4 pets can be live-owned at once.

**Care loop** (Home Room): Food, Social, and Health bars (0-100), each paired with a plain-language feelings word at low and high values (e.g. Food low = "Hungry," high = "Full") rather than just a number. Stats decay softly, only while the student is actively in Town Square (never while they're away), floored at 20 so a pet is never neglected to zero, and pets never die. A student feeds, pets, and plays with their pet from a care card; a pet can be renamed anytime and sold back for 40% of its price (with a confirm-tap safety) if a student's 4-pet home is full.

**Companion/follow mechanic**: a pet unlocks "walk beside you" in Town Square only after 5 logged task completions (`PET_FOLLOW_TRAINING_THRESHOLD`), tracked by the same counter used for the ABA shaping ladder (see A26). Training comes exclusively from real learning, never from clicking care buttons repeatedly: every finished assignment is +1, and (since the 2026-10-06 pets review) every 10 right answers anywhere (native games, Quiz mode, quizzes, the gas pump) is +1 too. Only one pet can be the active companion at a time.
