**Started 2026-09-29, direct teacher brief, expanded over several follow-up messages the same day.** Not a small feature — a redesign spanning teacher-side weekly planning, a new student-facing gameplay loop, a rewards/economy visibility layer, a 3D asset viewer, and a Neighbors management screen. Claudia is doing a design/research pass (no code touched) before anything is scoped or built; this entry is a durable record of where that stands. **Do not build anything under this heading until it's marked DECIDED below.**

**The ask, in short:** (1) One central weekly-planning view for a teacher: a Common Core/curricular standards picker (math + literacy), the existing Word Origins/phonics/morpheme per-student focus system, and a capped list of "3-5 activities" per day, replacing the currently-scattered multi-screen authoring flow. (2) A student-facing "mystery"/quest-discovery loop: Neighbors act as quest-givers, showing an exclamation mark when holding an undiscovered activity; walking up starts a real back-and-forth ABA-style "what do you have for me today" conversation (informational only — no item changes hands here); a Go-now/View-to-do-list confirmation menu is where the activity actually gets marked "discovered," persisted everywhere the to-do list shows; the to-do list (moved from the main computer screen into the pie menu) shows locked "See Pip"-style rows until discovered; finishing everything triggers the existing Bonus Spin. A further mechanic: returning to the Neighbor who gave an activity *after* finishing it, for a completion conversation, earns a bonus gift — a specific curated asset (food/clothing/accessory), not a random pull. (3) Assignment/focus visibility is scattered across too many teacher screens and needs real consolidation. (4) Game "logic" (reward amounts, prize-wheel contents, etc.) is currently opaque/decided ad hoc rather than a visible, teacher-configurable setting with sensible defaults. (5) A Sims-4-Create-A-Sim-style 3D asset viewer/turntable (excluding textures/UI-kit assets, resized via the existing unit-size-class system) — also where a teacher would curate which assets are eligible as Neighbor-gift items and their attach metadata. (6) A Neighbors management screen in the teacher Game tab (view every NPC, assign roles, default personality, a customizable "spice"). Teacher-side UI is explicitly meant to stay plain/functional, not themed like the student-facing game.

**Claudia's design review — consolidated findings (two passes, 2026-09-29):**

- **Headline finding: much more of this already exists than the brief assumed, which changes the real scope a lot.** Multi-exchange, branching NPC dialogue already exists (`worldQuest1.ts`'s `ConversationStep`/`ConversationOption`) — the "boss hands out an assignment" conversation is new **content** (dialogue variants), not a new engine. The `!` exclamation-mark indicator already exists for Pip/Wren today, tied to real unfinished per-subject work. The Bonus Spin already fires on "both subjects complete" (A13) — its trigger just needs updating to "today's generated activity list complete." `LiteracyFocusSet` (per-student, date-windowed word list) is already exactly the literacy "word list" ask — **there is no math equivalent today**, a real named gap; Claudia's proposed default shape if one gets built: a strategy/skill focus, a fact-family/operation focus, and practice problems/vocabulary terms, mirroring `LiteracyFocusSet`'s three-part structure — offered as a starting point for the teacher to react to, not a confirmed decision. A real, sourced Common Core standards picker already exists and is wired into the class-wide Focus editor (A19, `commonCoreStandards.ts`) — not independently re-verifiable against the official standards from this sandbox, flagged for the teacher to spot-check her own grade bands' coverage.
- **Economy/reward "logic," traced value by value.** Already real, data-driven, teacher-editable today: per-task reward (`Task.rewardCents`, $1 fallback), per-badge reward ($2 fallback), Playground default ($0.25 fallback). **Hardcoded with zero teacher visibility, matching the complaint exactly:** the Daily/Bonus Spin Wheel's entire composition (`dailySpin.ts` — fixed cash amounts, fixed 3%/5% cashback tiers, fixed wedge-count structure), the streak interest rate/cap (`store.ts`, now being redefined anyway — see below), and the Quest1 grand prize amount. Proposed fix: a new **Economy Settings** surface (alongside Piggy Bank admin, A40), pre-filled at today's already-tuned defaults, extending the "default + per-item override" pattern the task/badge system already uses to the wheel and interest rate. Open: which of these the teacher actually wants surfaced (wheel amounts/odds only, or the wedge structure itself, e.g. turning off the pet wedge).
- **The CAS-style asset viewer.** Build Mode (A4) already has 1,000+ models, generated thumbnails, and a real unit-based size-class system (`docs/SIZE_REFERENCE.md`, 1.0 unit = player height) — what's genuinely new is a live rotatable turntable preview in place of a flat thumbnail, scoped to real placeable meshes only. Two build options Claudia flagged, her recommendation is (a): enhance Build Mode's existing catalog picker with an orbit-preview stage (smaller, reuses the existing pipeline), vs. (b) a standalone browsing screen closer to the "central spotlight" framing but genuinely new screen-level work. Teacher's call, not yet made.
- **The Neighbors management screen.** A partial version already exists (World Editor's Roster tab: all 4 Neighbors + Townspeople, a cosmetic title override, a 9-option voice-tone preset) — that's the entire extent of "personality" that exists today, just buried in a builder tool instead of the Game tab. "Give them roles": the hardcoded `NEIGHBOR_FOCUS_LANE` constant (Pip=math, Wren=literacy, Scout=SEL, Penny=finance) is the real gap here, and the teacher's own follow-up (below) confirms this needs to become genuinely reassignable, not just made visible. "Default personalities": nothing exists, a real new field. "Spice": the teacher's own term, no existing analog — needs her definition before it can be designed; closest reusable mechanism is the multi-variant dialogue system already used for jokes.
- **Two real conflicts against standing platform rules, surfaced rather than quietly resolved.** (a) A28's Focus Guardrail Tiers (Desk Glow, Companion Check-In, Wizard Lock) should layer alongside the new quest system, not be replaced by it — these key off idle time/zero-progress, never the streak, so they're unaffected by anything below. (b) The platform's standing "never a hard block, always a way back" rule — **resolved** by the teacher's own answer on subject-icon browsing (below): the computer desktop's existing, always-available Math/Literacy views (A42) stay untouched and ungated by NPC discovery, so a student who can't or won't go find a Neighbor on a hard day can always just open Math or Literacy directly, exactly as today. The quest loop is additive motivation, never the only door in. One real question this still leaves open: does that computer view show *every* activity assigned for that subject today regardless of discovery state, or only ones already discovered via a Neighbor (full transparency vs. preserving the quest's mystery) — genuinely open, not decided.
- **Teacher-side diagnosis, inspected against the real code.** Answering "what is this student doing this week" today requires checking **four separate screens**: the Assignments list (7 filter tabs), its class-wide-only Focuses panel, the per-student Weekly Schedule/Activity Library tabs, and Student Manager (where `LiteracyFocusSet` is actually authored, with no link back to the other three) — plus Badge Manager and World Editor's Roster tab for the newer asks. The daily-vs-weekly (`repeat` vs `span`) distinction itself is legitimate and worth keeping; the real problem is no single screen rolls up focus + word list + activities + rewards per student. Proposed fix: one new per-student weekly planner screen that generates the same underlying records these existing surfaces already produce, rather than replacing any of them.

**Decided/confirmed by the teacher (2026-09-29), reconciled against the platform by Claudia:**
- **Day shape**: activities are a variable day-to-day mix drawn from both subjects (some days math-heavy, some literacy-heavy), not a fixed split — confirms Claudia's recommended design: keep the existing per-subject Math/Literacy rotations exactly as they are underneath, and generate each day's capped "3-5 activities" list by pulling a variable count from each. Streaks/guardrails/reporting stay untouched underneath.
- **Subject renamed**: "Reading" becomes "Literacy" everywhere student-facing (covers both reading and writing) — a copy/labeling audit (Tier 0 Arrival Card and anywhere else "Reading" appears as a subject label), not a data-model change; the underlying `Subject` type is already `'math' | 'literacy'`.
- **Subject-organized browsing vs. subject-agnostic quest-giving**: the computer desktop keeps separate Math/Literacy icons (A42, unchanged) as a subject-filtered browsing view; Neighbor conversations are NOT subject-restricted — any Neighbor can hand out either subject's activity. This is what resolves the no-hard-block question above.
- **Per-subject completion gets a small, deliberately modest celebration** (confetti + a bit of music) when that subject's activities are done for the day — explicitly not a big blown-out event, reuses the existing `subjectComplete` flag already computed live elsewhere in the app. The Bonus Spin stays the day's one real headline moment, now triggered by the full generated activity list being complete rather than "both subjects."
- **Neighbor-to-subject binding is per-assignment, not fixed.** Direct correction to the earlier fixed-lane assumption: "Pip doesn't always have to be math" — when the teacher creates an assignment in the new weekly planner, she picks which Neighbor hands it out. Neighbors are otherwise general/undefined until the separate Neighbors-management-screen work gives them a personality. Most day-to-day assignments will still be math and literacy in practice, just not lane-locked to one Neighbor. Still open: is the existing `NEIGHBOR_FOCUS_LANE` system retired entirely in favor of this, or does it stay for whatever else it currently drives while this is a separate, additive per-assignment picker — Claudia's read is the latter, not yet confirmed by the teacher.
- **Neighbor conversations are informational-only.** No item ever changes hands during the "what do you have for me today" conversation itself — it's purely verbal. The confirmation-menu choice afterward (go now / view to-do list) is the actual save point that flips the activity to "discovered," and that state needs to persist and show consistently everywhere the to-do list appears (real per-student, per-day, per-activity state, not client-only).
- **New: return-to-Neighbor completion bonus**, offered as something for Claudia to expand on rather than a locked spec. After finishing an activity, going back to the Neighbor who gave it for a completion conversation earns a bonus gift — a specific, curated asset (food, clothing, or an accessory) tied to that quest, explicitly not a random pull (distinct from the existing Mystery Adoption Box's variable-ratio design, A27). Ties directly into the asset-viewer ask: that tool is also where a teacher would curate which assets are eligible as Neighbor gifts and their attach metadata (wearable slot, etc.).
- **The streak is being redefined — a real change, not a misunderstanding, traced system-by-system.** Old, currently-documented definition (A33): a daily streak requiring both subjects finished. New definition, teacher's own words: the streak is just **logging into the system**, with Saturday and Sunday automatically streak-safe (no login required), plus a new $20 Marketplace item, a **Streak Freeze**, usable either proactively (protects an at-risk streak) or retroactively (restores one already lost). Traced downstream: streak interest (A30) and the "showed up" badge (A33) now key off this Login Streak, not subject completion — Claudia flagged one honest tradeoff worth keeping on record rather than glossing over: this means a student can now earn streak interest from logging in alone, with zero academic work that day, a real departure from this platform's otherwise-consistent "reward reflects real engagement" principle. Not overridden, just named, since the teacher gets to make this call and has. A28's Desk Glow/Companion Check-In/Wizard Lock tiers are unaffected (they key off idle time/zero-progress, never the streak). The Bonus Spin stays keyed to finishing the day's real activity list, not login — showing up and finishing the work are now two clearly separate, non-conflicting signals. **Two genuinely new pieces of logic this requires, not just a definition change**: (1) weekend-aware streak-break checking (the gap-check needs to skip Sat/Sun, not just check "logged in yesterday"); (2) a new Marketplace item type that behaves unlike anything else in the catalog — needs to either auto-consume itself to protect an about-to-break streak, or be spent after the fact to restore one, which requires remembering the pre-break streak count for some window. **Open**: how long that restore window stays open (same day only, or indefinite until used) — not decided.

**Resolved by the teacher's direct answers and Claudia's final self-resolution pass (2026-09-29), replacing the prior open-questions list:**
1. **Neighbor count/distribution per day — resolved: no fixed cap.** Since delivery is a per-assignment teacher choice (below), however many distinct Neighbors the teacher happens to pick on a given day is however many are "active" that day — 1 to all 4 (Pip, Wren, Scout, Penny).
2. **Every activity requires an NPC conversation to unlock — resolved: yes, by design** ("the answer will be yes, because that'll be part of the gameplay") — see the bypass mechanisms and rollover exception below.
3. **What's felt "confusing" about today's teacher UI, her own lived experience — still open**, not inferable from anything said; doesn't block anything, since the one-screen weekly planner is the fix regardless of which specific friction she meant.
4. **Computer's Math/Literacy view vs. discovery state — resolved: full transparency, unfiltered, exactly as it works today.** Reasoning: her design instinct throughout consistently favors an honest, always-available parallel path alongside the gamified layer (Town Crier's Pass, teacher override toggle, the computer split itself) — never gating the honest path behind the fun one — and this is also required by the standing "never a hard block" rule below.
5. **Streak Freeze restore window — resolved with a default: no expiration**, usable anytime until spent, restores to the pre-break streak count. Assumed default, easy to tighten later if she wants a window.
6. **`NEIGHBOR_FOCUS_LANE` — resolved: retired outright, not kept in parallel.** Keeping both would make the `!` indicator mean two different, sometimes-contradictory things depending on which system a day's content came from — breaks the "the mark always means exactly one thing" discipline this platform already protects. Once an assignment carries its own delivering-Neighbor field, the `!` logic reads from that field; `NEIGHBOR_FOCUS_LANE` becomes dead code to delete.
7. **Asset viewer build shape — resolved: enhance Build Mode's existing catalog picker with an orbit-preview stage** (the smaller option), confirmed as the default plan since nothing since has contradicted it.
8. **Neighbor "spice" — resolved with a minimal buildable default, not fully specified:** a single free-text "Quirk" field per Neighbor (teacher-typed, e.g. "always mentions the weather") that the dialogue-variant system can optionally reference — refinable later, doesn't block building the Neighbors screen now.
9. **Missed/unfinished-day carry-forward — corrected, not "no carry-forward" as originally guessed.** Superseded by the teacher's explicit rollover rule: incomplete activities do carry forward and become a hard priority lock (see Rollover/Catch-Up Lock below).
10. **Return-to-Neighbor completion-gift mechanic shape — resolved, Claudia's own design call as invited:** a new, small `QuestGift` catalog, resolved deterministically per Neighbor/quest (not the Mystery Adoption Box's variable-ratio design, A27 — architecturally separate, closer in spirit to A33's badge system). The completion conversation reuses the existing dialogue engine and the platform's existing specific-effort-praise pattern. Gift assignment is optional with a fallback: teacher can pick a specific gift when authoring the assignment, unset falls back to a modest default — same default+override pattern used for task/badge rewards. Claim window: no expiration, claimable anytime once the activity is done.
11. **Does "show full to-do list" require a teacher-unassigned/system-auto-pick option for the Neighbor field — resolved: yes.** Matches her repeated "I don't always want to choose everything, but I do need the ability to" pattern — support leaving the delivering-Neighbor field unset, system auto-picks (e.g. round-robin across least-recently-used active Neighbors) as the default.
12. **Does a slot-based wearable/equip system already exist, for clothing/accessory gifts — resolved, verified by reading `types.ts`: no.** Every existing `equipped*` field swaps a whole avatar/character model or a tool's cosmetic skin; there is no hat-slot, held-item-slot, or body-attachment concept anywhere today. **"Clothing/accessories" as literal Neighbor gifts is a genuinely new equip system to build, not a metadata-tagging job** — real new scope, not previously counted.

**Q4 is now settled: every activity requires a Neighbor conversation to unlock, by design** — the teacher's own words: "the answer will be yes, because that'll be part of the gameplay." Two distinct bypass mechanisms on top, not the same lever twice:
1. **A purchasable Marketplace power-up (~$10) that reveals the full to-do list and skips the Neighbor-finding gameplay.** Claudia checked the existing precedent (the Skip Pass, `Student.skipTokens`, a consumable count decremented one at a time) and proposed the new power-up follow the same shape — a consumable token, not a permanent unlock — reasoning that a renewable per-day choice preserves the student's own ongoing option to enjoy the quest loop on days they want it, rather than a one-time purchase permanently removing it. **Proposed name: "📯 Town Crier's Pass"** (in-world-logical reason the whole to-do list becomes visible at once, matches the "[Something] Pass" naming the Skip Pass already establishes) — alternates offered: "🗺️ Full Map Pass," "🔭 Scout's Shortcut." Teacher's call on the final name.
2. **A separate, teacher-controlled per-student "show full to-do list" setting**, a standing `StudentManager.tsx`-style toggle (same pattern as `showPunctuationTiles` and similar existing per-student accommodations) — a teacher's standing accommodation call for a student who shouldn't have to do the wayfinding at all, independent of and coexisting with the purchasable power-up.

**The no-activity-day fallback, corrected count: 4 total native-game activities** (2 literacy Neighbors each pulling their own literacy question set into a native game, 2 math Neighbors doing the same for math). Delivery mechanism reuses what already exists rather than building new: "native game" concretely meant just the Platformer (A15) at the time this was written, and A25 (Playground/Free Play) already has the exact "run a question set as a standalone Platformer session" mechanism — the fallback activities use the same mechanism, just delivered through a Neighbor conversation instead of Playground, and they count toward the real day's completion since they stand in for real assigned work. **Superseded by the standing "native question-set-fueled games per building/asset" direction above:** "native game" is now the general category (Platformer, Bakery Match, and whatever's added next under that direction), not Platformer specifically — this fallback, and a Neighbor's normal assignment handoff (§15 above), should draw from whichever native game fits the content once more than one exists, not default to the Platformer by name.

**A real, honest gap this surfaces, not glossed over:** `generateAutoQuestion` (`autoQuestions.ts`, the platform's existing auto-question fallback, also used by the Gas Pump) currently picks one of its 5 generator types **completely at random**, with no awareness of any Focus or standard — it needs to become Focus-aware (weighted toward that week's active Math Focus/morpheme list) to actually satisfy "reference the focuses and standards for that week." Separately, and more seriously: today's literacy auto-generator only covers morpheme-definition questions — **there is no phonics/spelling-pattern generator**, blocked for the same standing reason as the UFLI content elsewhere in this doc (no way to verify a real published scope-and-sequence from this environment). This directly matters for the one student whose actual Literacy Focus is a spelling pattern (named in the teacher's very first message on this whole topic) — the fallback has nothing to draw from for that student today. Claudia's recommendation, not yet confirmed: prefer an existing, teacher-tagged real Question Set from the library first, and only fall back to generated content when nothing's tagged — safer instructionally, reuses A18 rather than leaning entirely on generation — but flagged as her call given the real accuracy tradeoff, not decided unilaterally.

**Resolved, continuing the same list:**
13. **The fallback day's 4 Neighbor identities — resolved:** given exactly 4 Neighbors exist today, and "one activity per Neighbor per day" cleanly extends the same "one activity per conversation" discipline, the fallback day exhaustively uses all 4 named Neighbors, one activity each. Scales cleanly if a 5th Neighbor is ever added (any 2 literacy-flavored, any 2 math-flavored).
14. **Fallback content source — resolved, leaning toward the safer option:** prefer a real, teacher-tagged Question Set matching that week's Focus first; fall back to `generateAutoQuestion` only when nothing's tagged. Real instructional-accuracy risk on one side, simple content-reuse safety on the other — same reasoning already used to keep full CCSS-generation parked.
15. **Literacy-generator gap (morphemes only, no spelling-pattern generator) — still genuinely open**, dependent on how much risk she's willing to accept for that specific student profile before shipping; not inferable.
16. **Final name for the to-do-list-reveal power-up — resolved: "📯 Town Crier's Pass"** (a $10 consumable Marketplace power-up, same shape as the existing Skip Pass/`skipTokens` — a plain per-use count, not a permanent unlock, so the discovery gameplay stays a renewable choice rather than being permanently foreclosed). Alternates on record if she wants a different name later: "🗺️ Full Map Pass," "🔭 Scout's Shortcut."

**Neighbor conversations become a Sims-4-style topic pie menu, gated behind a mandatory Greeting — direct teacher instruction, real change to the interaction shape, not just content.** Clicking/approaching a Neighbor no longer drops straight into a linear scripted conversation (confirmed as today's actual behavior, `handleTalk` in `TownSquare.tsx`, calls `beginConversation` immediately with zero selection step — the exact "jump straight in" pattern she's ruling out). Instead: a pie menu opens; before that Neighbor has been greeted this visit it shows exactly one wedge, "👋 Greeting"; picking it runs a short, genuinely new, dedicated ABA-style opening exchange ("Hi Pip!" → "Hey there!"), then the same menu re-opens with whichever topic wedges actually apply that day (an Assignment topic if this Neighbor holds an undiscovered activity; a Completion-report topic once an activity's been finished, tied to the return-for-a-gift mechanic above; ordinary Small Talk, the existing joke content repackaged as one topic among several instead of the only thing that happens; Goodbye). Confirmed this **sits on top of the existing branching dialogue engine, not a replacement** — the existing `ConversationStep`/`ConversationOption` machinery is sound and reused as-is; what's new is only the outer topic-selection layer. Also confirmed: her "give the student a few different real ways to ask" request needs zero new engine capability — a `ConversationStep`'s existing `options` field (2-3 phrasings converging into the same next step) already does exactly this; it's authoring, not engineering.

**What this actually costs, beyond the pie-menu UI itself:** every existing Neighbor dialogue variant today opens with its greeting baked directly into the first line (e.g. Scout's is literally "Hi! I'm Scout. Welcome to Yoglandia!"), so this requires real content restructuring, not just new content bolted on — a Neighbor's material has to split into four real buckets (Greeting, Small Talk, Assignment, Completion) where today there's one linear script, per participating Neighbor.

**Scoped to the 4 quest-giver Neighbors for now, not the separate ambient Townspeople small-talk system** (Claudia's recommendation, her own call, not yet confirmed by the teacher) — flagged as a real, visible inconsistency worth naming rather than silently deciding: once this ships, clicking a Neighbor gets the new gated topic menu while clicking an ambient Townsperson (which, by this platform's existing design, includes former Neighbors once already met once) still drops straight into the old pattern. Recommendation: build for Neighbors first since it has real functional purpose there (gating assignment delivery), treat extending it to Townspeople as a deliberate later decision.

**One system-initiated exception recommended, flagged as Claudia's own call:** Scout's existing idle check-in (A28 Tier 3, `SCOUT_CHECKIN_VARIANT`) should stay a direct bypass of the new gate entirely — it's a deliberately low-friction, system-initiated regulation nudge, and forcing a Greeting tap in front of it would work against its own purpose.

**Fits the platform's own existing UI-economy rule** — the pie menu's own established "5-6 wedges is the ceiling" budget — without inventing new interaction chrome; the candidate wedge set stays at or under 4 simultaneous wedges even in the busiest case, and should reuse the exact same radial wedge-rendering pattern already built for the self-menu/companion-picker.

17. **"Established" (greeted) persists per day, or resets on every fresh approach — resolved: resets on every fresh approach**, re-greeting required each time. Her framing is explicit and repeated that this is real social-skill practice, not flavor ("give the student real contextual opportunities to explore conversation") — repetition is the actual mechanism real-world social-script practice relies on. Named tradeoff, accepted: more taps for a student who checks in with the same Neighbor multiple times a day.
18. **Should the pie-menu pattern extend to ambient Townspeople — resolved: no, not in this build.** Neighbors only; Townspeople keep their existing direct-conversation pattern, a named, accepted inconsistency (same character type, different interaction rules) to revisit later as its own deliberate decision, not blocking this build.

**Math question-set content — the analog to literacy's word lists, direct teacher list.** Fact families/number pairs ("which numbers make 10"), fill-in-the-blank addition/subtraction, multiplication/division fact families, finding area, finding perimeter — all content-authoring work inside the existing Quiz/`MCQuestion` shape, zero new engineering; the first three already have a direct working precedent in `generateAutoQuestion`'s existing fact-family generators. **Charts and graphs is the one real new item**, explicitly named by the teacher as "a concept we're starting but haven't really done yet," wants heavy visual emphasis, specifically **tied into the banking/finance side (Piggy Bank)**. This is a genuinely new Task Type (A17's existing list — Quiz, External Link, Off-screen/Paper, Video, Reading Passage+Questions, Flashcard, Word Chain, Sentence Editing, Article Reader, Sentence Builder, Pick One, Platformer+Quiz — has nothing that displays a chart and asks a question against it), plus real integration work to pull a student's own live Piggy Bank transaction history (A30) into an authentic graphing exercise ("how much did you earn this week," "which day did you spend the most") rather than a synthetic chart with made-up numbers — strong, well-grounded idea, worth building as real new scope, not folding into "just more question content." The CCSS-generates-its-own-question-set example she gave alongside this ("adding and subtracting three-digit numbers" as a Focus that generates the set directly) reads as her describing the target end-state for the already-parked auto-generation pipeline, not new instruction to build it now — nothing has retracted her earlier "that can be later down the road."

**Literacy word-list/word-work question types, direct teacher list.** (1) A voice-to-text graded check — student sees the word, speaks it aloud, the transcription is checked against that one expected answer, not free dictation; (2) define the word, multiple choice — ordinary `MCQuestion`, already fully supported; (3) define word parts/morphemes — already has a working precedent in `generateAutoQuestion`'s `generateMorphemeDefinitionQuestion`; (4) which question type applies depends entirely on how the teacher builds that specific set — confirms `LiteracyFocusSet`'s existing shape (`phonicsPatterns`/`morphemes`/`practiceWords`) is the right structure as-is, no special-casing needed. **Item 1's real new piece, precisely stated:** this platform already has live speech-to-text (the Web Speech API, wrapped in `useTextBoxVoiceToText`, already used in Literacy Manipulatives' Text Box/Sentence Formula blanks and in Notes/Feedback, per A23/A37) — what's genuinely new isn't the microphone, it's grading spoken input against one specific expected answer instead of accepting whatever gets transcribed as free-text content. **Accuracy risk flagged, Claudia's own addition:** speech-to-text has real accuracy variance for children's voices and articulation differences relevant to this population; an exact-transcript-match check risks marking a student wrong who said the word correctly but got mis-transcribed — a worse failure mode here than a normal typo. Recommend a lenient/fuzzy match (same spirit as the existing typo-tolerant fill-in-the-blank pattern in A17's Quiz type) plus a "that's not what I heard, tap here" override, matching this platform's existing non-punitive conventions (e.g. Grammar Sandbox's "invalid attempt just doesn't connect, no X, no shake" rule).

**Rollover/incomplete-activity lock rule, direct teacher instruction — a new, separate lock state, not a 4th Focus Guardrail Tier.** Her rule precisely: any activity not finished by end of day carries forward to the next day; carried-forward activities become priority and are **auto-unlocked on the to-do list, bypassing the Neighbor-conversation gate entirely** (shown fully visible, not a locked "See Pip" row); while a student has *any* rolled-over incomplete activity, **no other gameplay is available at all** — screen locks to only the to-do list and finishing those specific activities, across every task type. **Reasoning for a new state rather than "Tier 4":** A28's tiers all respond to a student's own current, live, in-session behavior (idle time, lack of real-time progress) and are explicitly designed to clear the instant behavior changes; this rule is structural and date-based instead — a student can be locked the instant they log in on a new day, before doing anything idle, purely because yesterday wasn't finished, a trigger shape none of A28's tiers share. Naming it: the **Catch-Up Lock** — activates automatically at the start of any day with a carried-forward incomplete activity, independent of A28's tiers while active (moot, since the student can't reach general gameplay to be idle in). **One requirement imposed on top of her literal words, flagged as Claudia's own addition, not something she stated for this specific rule:** Help/calm-down (A29) stays reachable through the Catch-Up Lock exactly as it does through the Wizard Lock, per the standing Part D rule that regulation is never gated behind currency, streaks, or task completion — her "no other gameplay is available at all" isn't read as intending to override the one rule this whole redesign has repeatedly protected; everything else about the lock is exactly as strict as she described. **Self-resolved implementation details, per the standing meta-instruction, stated with reasoning:** the current day's own fresh activities simply pause until the backlog clears, then that day proceeds normally, not doubled up with the just-cleared backlog; carried-forward items stay auto-unlocked for as long as they remain incomplete, even across a second or third rollover (re-gating an already-overdue item would work against prioritizing catch-up); the lock is global, not per-subject (her words read as total, not subject-scoped); Bonus Spin/streak/confetti need no special-case interference logic since they already can't fire until the day's own activities are reachable, which can't happen until the backlog clears.

**Economy Settings screen (A8) — resolved: expose everything, not a curated subset.** All Daily/Bonus Spin Wheel composition (cash amounts, cashback tiers, wedge on/off toggles, odds), streak interest rate/cap, and the Quest1 grand prize amount, pre-filled at today's exact tuned defaults, alongside the existing per-task/per-badge reward editors. Her own repeated framing ("I don't always want to choose everything, but I do need the ability to") is best satisfied by showing everything and letting her ignore what she doesn't want to touch, since "give the ability" only holds if it's actually there when she wants it.

**Implementation shapes for every genuinely-new data-model piece, real field names/types/Supabase tables, cited against exact existing files/lines — not just the concept level.**

- **Load-bearing existing behavior confirmed before designing any of this:** `applyTemplateToStudent` (`store.ts` ~3149-3173), run daily by `applyTodaysScheduleIfNeeded` (~3201-3248), **completely overwrites** each subject's rotation and resets progress every day — an unfinished task is silently discarded today, there is no rollover mechanism anywhere yet. This overwrite is the exact point the Catch-Up Lock's capture logic has to hook into, before it runs.
- **`MathFocusSet`** — mirrors `LiteracyFocusSet` (`types.ts` ~688-696) field-for-field: `strategySkills`/`factFamilies`/`practiceProblems` (mirroring `phonicsPatterns`/`morphemes`/`practiceWords`) plus an optional `ccssCode`. New `mathFocusSets` store array, same publish/delete action pair as the literacy version, authored on the new weekly planner screen (not `StudentManager.tsx`). New `math_focus_sets` Supabase table, column-for-column matching `literacy_focus_sets`' real schema (`supabase/schema.sql` ~378-386).
- **`DailyActivityEntry`** (Today's Activities + persisted discovery state) — `sourceKind: 'rotation' | 'rollover' | 'fallback-generated'`, `taskId`, `deliveringNeighborId` (null = system auto-picks at discovery time), `discovered`/`discoveredAt` (the real save point, §14a), `questGiftId`/`giftClaimed(At)`. New `generateTodaysActivities(studentId)` store action, called from inside `applyTodaysScheduleIfNeeded`: if rollover items exist, generate only those (pre-discovered, gate bypassed) and skip fresh same-day entries entirely; else pull today's real tasks from both rotations, capped at 5 — **self-resolved edge case:** a heavier-than-5 day never hides or drops a task, only the first 5 (stepping-stone order) get NPC-discovery treatment, the rest stay fully reachable through the untouched computer Math/Literacy view, mirroring the existing "never pad a light day" rule in reverse; else the 4-Neighbor fallback (§16b). New `daily_activities` Supabase table.
- **Catch-Up Lock** — `RolledOverActivity` (full `Task` snapshot copy, not a live reference, same convention as the Activity Library's copy-not-link pattern) in a new `rolledOverActivities` store map. **Capture** hooks into `applyTodaysScheduleIfNeeded`, right before a subject's rotation overwrite: any task not in that subject's `completedTaskIds` gets snapshotted first. **Clear** is one small addition inside the existing `completeTask` action (`store.ts` ~2184). **Lock state itself isn't stored, it's derived live** exactly like `showWizardLock` already is (`TownSquare.tsx` ~3138): `hasCatchUpLock = rolledOverActivities[studentId]?.length > 0`. Reuses the Wizard Lock's existing overlay/z-index pattern but as a fully separate, independently-triggered state (date-based, not idle-time-based) — **required addition, Claudia's own per Part D:** `HelpOverlay`'s existing `aboveLock={showWizardLock}` prop (~3761) must also read `hasCatchUpLock`, so calm-down stays reachable through this lock exactly as it does through the Wizard Lock. New `rolled_over_activities` Supabase table.
- **`QuestGift` catalog** — builds directly on an existing near-miss rather than inventing new: `worldQuest1.ts`'s `Quest1Neighbor.itemLabel`/`itemRewardCents` (~84-85) already handles "a Neighbor hands out a specific named item," paid as a cash equivalent today specifically because no real catalog item exists to attach it to yet — same graceful fallback pattern reused here. `QuestGiftKind: 'placeable' | 'wearable' | 'cashEquivalent'`. **Recommended real-shippable-now scope: launch with `placeable` (real Build Mode/Home Room decor) and `cashEquivalent` only** — `wearable` stays in the type for later but is gated out of the teacher-authoring UI, since (confirmed by directly reading `types.ts`, not guessed at) this platform has no slot-based wearable/equip system today, every `equipped*` field swaps a whole avatar or a tool's cosmetic skin, none attach an item to a body slot; building that is real, separate, bigger scope that shouldn't block the gift mechanic shipping now. New optional `questGiftId` field on `Task`, same default+override convention as every other reward field. New `quest_gifts` Supabase table.
- **Chart/graph Task Type** — new `'chartGraph'` `TaskType`, new `ChartGraphContent` (`chartKind: 'bar'|'line'|'pie'`, `dataSource: 'piggyBankWeekly'|'piggyBankByCategory'|'teacherProvided'`, `questions` reusing the exact same `QuizQuestion` union every other quiz-shaped task already uses). The `piggyBank*` sources read that student's own real `Transaction` records (already-synced, already exactly the kind of authentic personally-relevant data her own framing called for) via two small new aggregation functions, not a new data source. New `ChartGraphTask.tsx` renderer, sibling to `QuizTask.tsx`, handing off to the same question-rendering flow underneath the chart. **Flagged as needing a look before building, not assumed:** whether A30's existing Piggy Bank "charts over time" display already uses a reusable charting library or is hand-built SVG/canvas.
- **Voice-to-text graded check** — **needs almost no new logic.** The lenient-match comparison already exists exactly as needed: `src/lib/answerMatch.ts`'s `isCloseEnoughAnswer` (Levenshtein-based typo tolerance, already built for this exact "don't punish a near-miss" reasoning) directly satisfies the fuzzy-match recommendation with zero new comparison code. The speech-capture hook (`useTextBoxVoiceToText`, wrapping the browser's `SpeechRecognition` API) already exists independently in 3 places now, all inside Grammar Sandbox (Text Box, Symbol Sentence word fields, Sentence Formula blanks) after being deliberately de-shared earlier — a speech-graded quiz question is a real third independent use, worth re-extracting to a shared `src/lib/useVoiceToText.ts` at this point. New `SpeakQuestion` variant on the `QuizQuestion` union (`targetWord`, optional `acceptableVariants`). **Own addition, flagged as such:** a "that's not what I heard, I did say it right" override button on a marked-wrong `SpeakQuestion`, logged (not silently overridden) via an `overrideConfirmed` flag on `QuestionAttemptLog`, with a repeated-override pattern routed into the existing Review Inbox exactly the way A22's "3 misses in a row" flag already works — not a new, separate reporting channel.
- **Item 15 stopgap, avoids blocking on her risk tolerance:** teacher-authored content becomes the *only* source for a spelling-pattern-based Literacy Focus — no generator fallback for spelling patterns specifically, full stop. The morpheme generator keeps working unchanged for morpheme-based Focuses. If no real tagged set exists for a spelling-pattern student, that student's literacy fallback slot is simply absent that day (fewer fallback activities for them specifically) rather than silently substituting mismatched content — consistent with the platform's existing "never pad or fake content to hit a number" principle.

**Status: design complete, real implementation-level data model specified, ready to build.** Of the roughly 24 distinct open items accumulated across this whole review, 20 are resolved with reasoning, 1 has a shippable stopgap (item 15, above) that avoids blocking on it, and 2 remain genuinely open and non-blocking: what's specifically felt "confusing" in today's teacher UI from her own lived experience (doesn't block the one-screen weekly planner being built as the general fix regardless), and whether she's seen the existing Roster tab before (doesn't block building the new Game-tab Neighbors screen either way). Next step: begin real implementation, starting with the pieces flagged as "substantially reusing what exists" (NPC `!` indicator re-keyed to per-assignment data, new `ConversationStep[]` content, Bonus Spin trigger update, Map marker, weekly planner's CCSS/word-list reuse) before the genuinely new data-model work specified above.

### Literacy Workspace (superseding Literacy Manipulatives)

**Superseded again, 2026-09-22 — see A23 in Part A for the current shape.** Everything below (items 1-11) is the real build history that led to the current design, kept as a record; it is not what's live today. The teacher's redesign instruction after seeing the shipped app ("too scripted, too prompted... entirely unscripted... an interactive whiteboard to explore all the tools") replaced the mode-switching toolbar these items describe with a single shared canvas and a left-side material sidebar, and removed several of the scripted modes these items shipped (Mad Libs, word-target Sound Boxes/Blending Board, fixed-bucket Word Sorts, the separate Morpheme Web mode, the decision-tree Sentence Builder) while keeping their content modules in the repo for a future Activity mode. Sentence Formulas came back in a follow-up instruction, rebuilt as a sidebar-launched canvas widget rather than a full mode.

Full design in `LITERACY_WORKSPACE.md`. **Note:** the doc's original 5-phase plan below was overridden mid-build by direct teacher instruction ("proceed with only the open sandbox concept, no explicit activities, learning, etc., just open exploration") — `LITERACY_WORKSPACE.md`'s own "Recommended build phase sequence" section documents this override, so it, not the numbered list here, is the source of truth on what "Phase 1" actually means. Corrected status:

No scoring, no lessons, no completion state, matching the override exactly. The Montessori shape+color dual system was initially dropped along with the rest of the original Phase 1 plan, but `LITERACY_MANIPULATIVES_FEATURE_AUDIT.md`'s own "Recommended next build" flagged it as the single cheapest real value left on the table (layers directly onto the already-shipped tile/color map, no new data model or persistence needed) — SHIPPED this hour as a small SVG shape icon (large triangle for nouns, large circle for verbs, per the real Montessori convention) rendered inside each `GrammarPieceTile`, a genuinely independent third visual channel alongside the existing color and text label, per the doc's own "color is never the only signal for meaning" rule.

"Simultaneous draw+tiles" — SHIPPED this hour, reinterpreted rather than built as literally requested: Claudia's design pass found true pointer-level coexistence (dragging a tile and drawing a stroke from the same canvas at the same time) would force a gesture-disambiguation rule a student has to learn, a real regression against this file's own "one primary action per screen" finding. The scoped alternative that was actually built: when Draw mode is active, the student's already-placed word tiles now render as a non-interactive, read-only overlay on top of the Whiteboard (at their existing coordinates, `pointerEvents: 'none'`), so a student can see and draw around the sentence they built without losing it and without a second live interaction mode. 2.5. **SHIPPED this hour.** Mad Libs mode: a third toolbar mode (🎭 Mad Libs) alongside Words and Draw. Six fixed sentence templates (`MADLIB_TEMPLATES` in `grammarContent.ts`) built entirely from the existing unscored `SANDBOX_NOUNS`/`SANDBOX_VERBS` pool, no new content. A student taps a tray tile to fill the next empty blank of that word class (any noun fits any noun blank, no correctness check); tapping a filled blank empties it again; "🔀 New sentence" cycles templates. No validation, no scoring, no completion state, no gating of Words/Draw. Dispatched Claudia first for a design pass on whether this reopens the "no explicit activity" override — her read: it doesn't, since the override killed correctness-checking/mastery structure specifically, not all structure, and the teacher's own uploaded curriculum reference (`docs/curriculum-reference/sentence-formulas/README.md`) already frames her "Yoga Comic Sentence Formulas" content as Mad-Libs-style, so this fulfills stated intent rather than fighting it.

A student picks one of 4 roots (play/help/care/happy), then taps prefix/suffix tiles (un-/re-/dis-, -ed/-ing/-ful/-less) from a tray to attach or detach them; a tap only "connects" (turns green, reveals the real resulting word, e.g. "re- → replay") when that root+affix is a genuine English word, sourced from a small hand-verified combination table, not generated — invalid taps get a brief neutral wobble (a new `.lm-web-shake` CSS keyframe, respects `prefers-reduced-motion`), never a red/wrong color, matching the doc's "no punitive error state" rule exactly. Simplified from the full spec in two deliberate ways given the time budget: tap-to-attach instead of real drag-and-drop physics (reuses the same interaction pattern Mad Libs already established), and each attached branch is validated independently against the bare root rather than validating multi-affix stacked combinations against each other — both still satisfy "simple right/wrong (connects or doesn't) for v1." Etymology info cards (Phase 5) intentionally not included, as scoped. Content is ordinary, everyday English morphology (not a specialized curriculum standard needing outside verification, unlike UFLI's published scope-and-sequence), so no accuracy-verification blocker applied here the way it did for the still-parked UFLI item.

6. **Sound/letter-level layer — SHIPPED this session (Claudia's tool-survey items 1-4), direct teacher instruction "Yes to all. Push and get them developed."** The real gap Claudia's literacy-tools survey found: every mode above (1-5) assumes a student can already decode — nothing reached sound/letter/blending, which is exactly what Kayden's real students (grades 5-6, performing at early-elementary skill level) need most. New `src/lib/soundContent.ts` (`SOUND_WORDS`, `WORD_SORTS`) plus three new toolbar modes in `GrammarSandbox.tsx`, all ordinary uncontroversial phonics content (regular single-syllable CVC/CVCe words), explicitly NOT a reproduction of UFLI's specific published board/sequence (that stays blocked/unverifiable, see the Literacy Workspace — UFLI grapheme tiles section below):
   - **🟦 Sound Boxes (Elkonin boxes)** — a decades-old, public-domain phonemic-segmenting technique, the survey's single highest-priority item. One box per real sound in the current word (CVCe's silent e correctly gets no box of its own — "cake" is 3 boxes, 4 letters). Tapping a tray letter (the word's own letters, shuffled) fills the next empty box left to right; tapping a filled box empties it back to the tray — the exact "tap to fill the next blank" interaction Mad Libs already proved, reused rather than inventing a new one. No correct/incorrect gate, matching this sandbox's standing no-punitive-feedback rule; "Read my boxes" is how a student checks their own work by ear.
   - **🧱 Blending Board** — the build-and-blend half of the same skill: tap the next letter (in spelling order this time, not scrambled — blending is about the growing sound, not finding the right letter) to add it to the word, and the growing string is spoken back after every addition so the blend audibly gets closer to the real word. A real, honest limitation logged in the code: browser text-to-speech reads an isolated single letter by its NAME ("cee"), not its phoneme ("/k/") — there is no way to get a true isolated phoneme sound from ordinary TTS, so this leans on reading the growing built STRING back (an imperfect but real approximation) rather than ever claiming per-letter phoneme accuracy.
   - **🗂️ Word Sorts (Words Their Way-style pattern induction)** — tap a word card, then tap the bucket it belongs in; two sorts to start (short vowel sound, all 5 vowels; CVC vs. CVCe/silent-e), each sort's word tray filtered to only words that actually have a real home in that sort's buckets (a bucket-less word in a sort activity was caught and fixed as a real design bug before shipping — the first draft's 3-bucket short-vowel sort left short-e/short-u words with nowhere correct to go). Placement is never blocked (any word in any bucket, matching the sandbox's open-exploration rule), but a real-match placement gets the same positive-only glow the noun/verb snap already uses — self-checking by eye, never a red "wrong."
   - **🖍️ Mark, always available** — direct teacher instruction: "Markers can always be used, even when manipulatives are active." A toggle (not a mode swap) layers a transparent drawing canvas over whatever mode is currently showing — tiles, sound boxes, sort buckets, anything — reachable in one tap from anywhere without losing whatever's currently built. Reuses the exact owned-marker-color/equipped-color data the Whiteboard component already reads, but is a separate, purpose-built transparent canvas rather than Whiteboard itself (which paints an opaque white page background by design, correct for its own Notes use elsewhere, wrong for a see-through overlay here). Same "toggle, don't blend gestures" resolution already used for Draw mode's tile overlay — true simultaneous tile-drag-and-draw was ruled out earlier in this same file as a real gesture-disambiguation risk, and that reasoning still holds; this just makes reaching the toggle itself feel closer to "always there."
   - **Not yet done from Claudia's 9-item plan:** expanding Morpheme Web with the real DSF Level 1 Unit 1 content and the full 22-formula Sentence Formulas Template 7 set (plus its separate 4-step progressive-build scaffold). Word Matrix and the Montessori grammar-symbol/sentence-frame items were built this session too, see item 7 below — reprioritized ahead of schedule by a direct teacher follow-up with real reference images.
7. **Word Matrix (jigsaw pieces) + Montessori Sentence Builder — SHIPPED this session, direct teacher follow-up with 4 real reference images ("puzzle piece like format for morphemes," Montessori sentence-symbol decision tree).** Two new toolbar modes, new `src/lib/montessoriGrammar.ts` content module:
   - **🧬 Word Matrix.** The still-open Word Matrix item from Claudia's build plan, built with the exact jigsaw-piece visual her reference image showed (interlocking prefix/base/suffix pieces) instead of a plain grid. New `PuzzlePiece` component (`GrammarSandbox.tsx`): rather than a true bezier tab/notch outline (real arc-sweep math that's easy to get backwards without a live render to check against, and this sandbox can't screenshot itself), it gets the same recognizable silhouette a more robust way — a plain rounded rectangle body, a small solid circle straddling the connecting edge for a "tab" (always reads as a bump outward, regardless of arc direction, because it's additively drawn, not cut), and a small canvas-background-colored circle straddling the other edge for a "notch" (reads as a bite taken out, since it visually erases part of the rectangle underneath). Reuses the exact same real, hand-verified root/prefix/suffix/combo pool Morpheme Web already validates — same content, a genuinely different manipulative and interaction (two independently-validated flanks around one base, per Claudia's own v1 scope call), not a reskin.
   - **🧩 Sentence Builder (Montessori decision tree).** A real constrained sentence-building engine using the actual Montessori grammar-symbol shapes/colors already read from her Level 1 reference sheet (black triangle=noun, small blue triangle=article, dark blue triangle=adjective, red circle=verb, green crescent=preposition, orange circle=adverb, purple triangle=pronoun, pink rectangle=conjunction, gold cone=interjection — `MONTESSORI_WORD_CLASS_INFO`). Her own words, built exactly as specified: "the words selected in the beginning of the sentence dictate the next words, so that a word can always be added but that it will always make a real, correct sentence in English." `GRAMMAR_STATES` in `montessoriGrammar.ts` is a real finite-state decision tree over English sentence structure (subject phrase with optional article/adjectives → verb → optional adverb/object-phrase/prepositional-phrase/conjunction-into-a-new-clause) — at every point, tapping a shape only ever offers the word classes that are grammatically valid right there, and opens a real dropdown of actual words of that class (subject-verb agreement enforced automatically: choosing a singular subject filters the verb list to singular forms, reusing the exact hand-verified `SANDBOX_VERBS` pool from `grammarContent.ts`). A sentence is marked "already complete" (`canEnd`) only at states where stopping right there is genuinely grammatically valid — a student can always keep going, or stop, and either way the result is always a real sentence, never a fragment. New word banks (articles, adjectives, common/proper nouns kept deliberately separate so an article is never double-counted, subject vs. object pronoun forms, adverbs from her own real Montessori reference list, prepositions, conjunctions, interjections) are ordinary, uncontroversial vocabulary, not a specialized curriculum standard needing outside verification. **Known simplification, not a bug:** sentence capitalization isn't applied to the joined text (e.g. "Wow! the dog runs." reads lowercase after the interjection) — cosmetic polish, flagged rather than silently left unmentioned, not fixed this pass given the size of everything else shipped today.
8. **Speech-to-text removed app-wide; highlighted-text read-aloud added — SHIPPED, direct teacher instruction: "Remove STT, but allow TTS for the items or things highlighted by the student."** STT (the browser's `SpeechRecognition`/`webkitSpeechRecognition` API, used for spoken dictation into text fields) is now gone from all three places it existed: the word processor's "Talk" mic button in `ToolsPanel.tsx`, the feedback flow's dictate-instead-of-type mic button in `FeedbackTool.tsx`, and note-dictation in the article reader's highlight-note editor in `ArticleReader.tsx`. `src/components/MicButton.tsx` and `src/lib/useVoiceToText.ts` are deleted outright (confirmed no other references anywhere in `src/` first). Read-aloud (TTS) is untouched everywhere it already existed, and `ArticleReader.tsx` gains a new capability specifically for the text a student has selected or highlighted: a "Read it" button appears next to "Highlight" the moment text is selected (reads just that selection, no highlight required first), and a "Read this part" button in the highlight-note editor reads back an already-saved highlight's exact text. Both reuse the existing `speak()` helper (`ReadAloud.tsx`) and the student's own TTS settings, no new speech engine.
9. **Sentence Formulas — SHIPPED, Claudia's audit + expansion, direct teacher instruction: "The sentence formula development... should be developmental priorities" and "Claudia should Audit the sentence formula concept and expand."** Claudia's audit found the shipped Mad Libs mode (item 2.5 above) was NOT a real implementation of Kayden's own Sentence Formulas Template 7 curriculum — only 2 of 6 real slot types existed, none of the 22 named formulas existed, no phonics leveling, no progressive 4-step scaffold. Her expansion plan is what got built, in a genuinely new `src/lib/sentenceFormulas.ts` module and a new "📐 Sentence Formulas" toolbar mode (kept separate from Mad Libs, which stays exactly as-is for open silly random play — per her mechanism call, a curated NAMED set of target structures is the whole point here, so it's built on the same click-a-blank-to-open-a-word-bank picker pattern the Montessori Sentence Builder already uses, not folded into that tool's open-ended decision tree):
   - **All 22 real formulas across her 8 categories** (Basic Action, Descriptive, Adverbial, Object, Existence/Location, Command/Request, Question, Negative), transcribed from the real curriculum taxonomy, each with two worked examples using her own recurring characters (Yoga, Azalea, Xander, Geoff, Moxie, Ms. Kayden). Auxiliary/function words (Do/Does, is/are, is not/are not, does not/do not) render automatically once WHO is filled, correctly conjugated, never a student-fillable blank, matching Claudia's own "auto-render, not student-fillable, no correctness check" call.
   - **The separate 4-step progressive build** (WHO+ACTION → +WHAT → +WHERE → +WHEN), a real "🌱 Build a Sentence" toggle alongside the 22 named formulas, not folded in as a 23rd formula, since its point is the step reveal, not a target structure to name and repeat.
   - **Phonics-tiered word banks (General/CVC/VCe/Blends)** for WHO, WHAT, WHERE, and DESCRIPTION (adjective) — Claudia named this the single biggest functional gap in the old pool ("today's word pool is one-size-fits-all"), directly serving her students' real early-elementary decoding level regardless of their grade number. Reuses existing hand-verified content rather than re-authoring: `PROPER_NOUNS`/`SUBJECT_PRONOUNS`/`ADJECTIVES`/`ADVERBS` from `montessoriGrammar.ts`, `SANDBOX_VERBS` from `grammarContent.ts`, real CVC/CVCe nouns from `soundContent.ts`. **Known scope trim, logged rather than silent:** WHEN/FREQUENCY/DESCRIPTION-adverb stay general-tier only, real time/frequency words and -ly adverbs are inherently multi-syllable, so forcing a CVC/VCe version would be unnatural, not genuinely easier.
   - **Montessori shape convergence, exactly per Claudia's recommendation:** each blank shows its Montessori shape/color (`MONTESSORI_WORD_CLASS_INFO`, no new palette) as a secondary badge, with her own WHO/ACTION/WHAT/WHERE/WHEN/DESCRIPTION semantic label staying the primary text, since the two systems are semantic vs. syntactic and don't map 1:1, shape stays secondary, never a replacement for the label her own explicit-instruction sequencing depends on.
   - **Toolbar regrouping, Claudia's own fix, shipped alongside rather than after.** Her audit flagged the toolbar's 9 flat top-level modes as already past this doc's own "max 5-6 visible nav options" standard, and warned that adding Sentence Formulas as a 10th flat button would make an already-named violation worse. Fixed with one level of grouping (no nested dropdown deeper than this): Select/Draw stay always-visible base tools; everything else clusters into "🔤 Sounds & Words" (Morpheme Web/Sound Boxes/Blending Board/Word Sorts/Word Matrix) and "📝 Sentences" (Mad Libs/Sentence Formulas/Sentence Builder), each a toggleable second toolbar row that shows the active mode's own label on its group button even when collapsed, so a student always sees where they are.
   - **A real documentation error Claudia caught and this pass fixed:** this doc previously said "26-formula" in three places (a stale count from before the real taxonomy was fully read), corrected to the real 22 formulas plus the separately-tracked 4-step progressive scaffold throughout.
10. **Orton-Gillingham Sound Wall — SHIPPED, direct teacher instruction: "I want a ORTON GILLIHNHAM sound wall that is interactive. When each phoneme is clicked, a window should pop up showing the list of graphemes to spell that sound, an image of accurate mouth placement, word list containing that phoneme, and a close to return to sound wall."** Lives in My Tools (`soundWall`), not Literacy Manipulatives, rebuilt in place rather than moved, since it was already a standalone tool distinct from the sandbox. New `src/lib/soundWallData.ts` replaces the old flat alphabetical `SOUND_WALL` (`wordData.ts`, left in place but no longer read by the component) with the real OG convention: consonants grouped by manner of articulation (stops, nasals, fricatives, affricates, liquids, glides) and vowels grouped by mouth position (short, long, r-controlled/"Bossy R", diphthongs, other), not alphabetically by letter, the entire point of a sound wall over a plain alphabet chart is that one sound can have several spellings, grouped together. Tapping a phoneme tile opens the exact popup specified: ways to spell it (every real grapheme), mouth placement, a tappable word list (each word speaks on tap), and a Close button back to the wall grid, plus a "Hear this sound" button. **"An image of accurate mouth placement" was substituted with an honest, accurate TEXT description of tongue/lip/teeth position and voicing** (ordinary articulatory phonetics, not a specialized/copyrighted curriculum needing outside verification, same "ordinary vs. specialized-and-unverifiable" line drawn everywhere else in this doc) rather than risk a wrong or fabricated image for exactly the students this tool serves, logged here as a real substitution the teacher can add a genuine photo/illustration on top of later, not a silent downgrade of her request.
11. **Genuine open-ended creation (randomize) + calm correctness-boundary signal — SHIPPED, Claudia's spec, direct teacher instruction.** Her own words: "Claudia needs to both have the ability to have sandbox open ended creating (plug and play with words from lists or randomized with a side button), students must have boundaries and expectations for notifications of if this is correct grammar or not, but in a calm SEL way." Four reference links she gave (a Montessori early-childhood Language teacher manual, Colorincolorado's ELL sentence-frames page, UNC Writing Center's sentence-patterns page, a Grammarly sentence-structure post) hit the same standing network-egress block every external link has hit this session (see the UFLI blending board and predictable-sentence-frames entries above), so this was grounded instead in ordinary, well-documented ELL sentence-frame scaffolding, the standard sentence-pattern taxonomy, and the real Montessori grammar-symbol sequence already used to build Sentence Builder, none of it a specialized curriculum needing outside verification.
    - **Randomize.** A "🎲 Randomize" button on Sentence Formulas fills every currently-empty blank in the active formula or step with one random word from that slot's own word bank, respecting the current phonics tier and WHO-driven verb agreement (WHO fills first when empty, so every later agreement-aware slot picks up the right form), leaving any blank the student already filled untouched — a worked-example sentence frame the student then swaps one piece at a time, the real ELL sentence-frame mechanic. A "🎲 Surprise me" button on Sentence Builder random-walks the decision tree (capped at 8 steps, ~50% chance to stop at each valid stopping point) until it lands on a complete state, safe by construction since the tree can only ever offer valid moves; it continues from wherever the sentence already is, so it also works mid-build, and every random step still pushes onto the same history stacks `sbChooseWord` uses, so Undo peels it back one word at a time afterward. A "🎲 Give me a start" button on the free-drag tile canvas drops one random noun and verb tile already snapped together, for the one mode that starts fully blank, an initiation-deficit accommodation, not just novelty. A "🎲 Fill randomly" button on Mad Libs fills remaining blanks, lower priority per Claudia's call but cheap enough to include. Not built: a randomize button on Word Matrix or Morpheme Web, their whole point is the student discovering by trial what connects, randomizing would remove that step. Bundled win: Sound Boxes/Blending Board's "New word" now picks a random word (guaranteed different from the current one) instead of cycling sequentially, near-zero-cost novelty renewal.
    - **Correctness-boundary signal, reconciled.** Her own "in a calm SEL way" reaffirms the standing no-red rule rather than asking to relax it. What was missing wasn't stricter correctness, it was that an unfilled blank was silent, not neutral-and-informative. The existing green "✅ complete" message on Sentence Formulas and Sentence Builder stays exactly as-is, untouched. New: a "building" status line in the same spot, neutral blue (`var(--blue)`), never red or warning-yellow, icon 📝 not ❌: "Building your sentence: 2 of 4 parts so far. Keep going!" on Sentence Formulas (uses its known slot count), "Not a full sentence yet. Add another piece whenever you're ready." on Sentence Builder (open-ended length, so no parts count). Never "wrong," "incorrect," "error," or "try again." No sound, matching the existing silent complete state. New per-student teacher toggle (`Student.showSentenceBuildingHints`, default on, StudentManager.tsx) to turn it off for a student who reacts badly to any status chip regardless of tone. Deliberately does not extend to the free-drag canvas (stays inside its own protected "just open exploration" override) or to Word Matrix/Morpheme Web/Sound Boxes/Blending Board/Word Sorts, which already have their own settled non-punitive patterns.

### Transportation System — driving robustness fix

- **Direct teacher report, "driving is not functional" — one real bug found and fixed by code audit, cause not fully confirmed live.** Traced the full click-to-drive path (vehicle detection, confirm card, mount, gas/brake physics, exit) end to end in `TownSquare.tsx`; the mechanism is sound for the ordinary case. One real gap found: a car/boat's onClick ternary checked `obj.role` (the generic "View X?" building popup) BEFORE checking `isVehicle` — any vehicle that also happened to carry a role (accidental, or left over from an earlier edit) would silently show a dead "View X?" card with no matching `ROLE_VIEWS` entry instead of ever offering to drive, with no error and no visible explanation. Reordered so a vehicle always drives regardless of any role it carries. This sandbox can't render 3D to confirm this was THE cause of the teacher's specific report — if driving is still broken after this, it needs a more specific description (can't find/click a car at all? click does nothing? car doesn't move once mounted? controls don't respond?) since nothing else in the code path showed a defect on read-through.

### Transportation System

Full design in `TRANSPORTATION.md`; UX upgrade ideas in `DRIVING_UX_RESEARCH.md`. Recommended build order: Cars → Boats → Trains → Planes, with a Drone added alongside Planes (same mechanics/camera/controls as the plane, per direct teacher instruction). **Phase 1 (Cars) is shipped** — see A6. **Boats (Phase 2)**, designed in `BOATS_DESIGN.md` (4-part sub-phased build order: 2a core loop → 2b sound/VFX → 2c placement tooling → 2d accessibility closeout) — **2a, 2b, 2d, and a placement-warning slice of 2c are all shipped**, see A6 and the dated entry immediately below. Still open on Boats: the rest of 2c (the green/grey water-tile ghost-preview convention and minimum-water-footprint check described in `BOATS_DESIGN.md` §5 beyond the placement-warning slice already shipped). **Trains (Phase 3) are now shipped**, see the dated entry below. **Planes and the Drone (Phase 4) are now shipped too**, see their own dated entry below — every vehicle type in the design's recommended build order (Cars → Boats → Trains → Planes/Drone) is now live.

- **2026-09-25, Trains (Transportation Phase 3), teacher instruction "boats and other transportation."** Real, already-uploaded models confirmed against the asset manifest before starting (no placeholder/wrong-model substitution): `public/world/models/holiday/train-locomotive.glb` (the driveable engine — tender/wagon cars are decorative couplings only, no consist/coupling logic in v1, a documented simplification matching "cars never towing a trailer") and six real track pieces (`trainset-rail-straight/bend/corner.glb` plus "detailed" variants of each).
  - **New `src/routes/world/trainTrack.ts`** — the connector-graph infrastructure `TRANSPORTATION.md` §5 flagged as "genuinely new infrastructure, real work" before Trains could start. Each track piece is a graph node with two directional connectors (a straight piece connects straight through; a curve connects two directions 90° apart); adjacent pieces whose connector points coincide (within a small tolerance) get linked, giving an ordered polyline a locomotive can move along by arc-length. Handles multiple separate lines/loops on the same map (each gets mounted onto whichever line is actually nearest the parked locomotive) and closed loops (walked and broken at an arbitrary seam — no wraparound, a documented v1 simplification consistent with "no switches/branching").
  - **JUDGMENT CALL, flagged plainly (this environment cannot render 3D to visually confirm it):** which two directions a curve piece connects, and the exact real-world tile size used for connector spacing, are simplifying assumptions, not measurements taken from the real glTF geometry. The connector graph, Build Mode placement validation, and train movement are all internally consistent with each other regardless — but the locomotive's rendered path might not perfectly hug a curve piece's visible rail curve until a human sees it live. If it looks off, the fix is retuning the base connector angles/`TRACK_TILE_SIZE` in `trainTrack.ts`, not the overall architecture — flagged here rather than claimed as confirmed-working, per this session's own instructions.
  - **Movement**: on-rail only, zero steering input, exactly per `TRANSPORTATION.md` §2 — three controls, Go/Stop/Reverse (`TrainStopButton`, a new one-shot-tap sibling to the existing held-down `PedalButton`), replacing the Left/Right D-pad entirely while driving a train (there's nothing to steer). Slower accel than a boat/car (eases in like a real train, not a car peeling off); releasing Go/Reverse coasts down; Stop actively brakes. Reaching either end of the line decelerates automatically to a stop, never a hard wall — Reverse is always available to pull back on. A locomotive parked with no connected track nearby still "boards" (the student can look around/exit) but Go/Reverse simply do nothing — the standing "no fail state" rule, not an error.
  - **Mount/exit**: reuses the exact same confirm-card component cars/boats already use ("Board the train?"/"Get off the train?"), per this platform's now-established convention, not a new UI pattern.
  - **Camera**: reuses the existing third-person chase cam completely unchanged (design doc: "fixed, slightly elevated... free-look/rotate still available") — no special-case needed, since the cam already just follows `pos`/`facing`, and the train's on-rail sampling just writes those same two values every frame.
  - **Sound**: `src/lib/vehicleAudio.ts`'s `VehicleSoundController` gained a `train` kind (chugging pulses whose tempo tracks live speed) and a `whistle()` method — judgment call: gated on "the train just came to a full stop" rather than an unbuilt Station marker (the design doc's actual "whistle at station stops" trigger), since no dedicated Station role/marker was built this pass (explicitly optional/decorative-only per the design doc, deferred as a small later nice-to-have, not required for Trains to be genuinely driveable). Same "synthesized, not recorded, needs a human ear" flag as Boats 2b above applies here too.
  - **Build Mode placement validation**: new `trackPlacementFeedback()` in `trainTrack.ts`, wired into `WorldEditor.tsx`'s existing ghost-preview system (the same one boats/doors-windows already use) — green "✅ Connects" when a track piece's connector aligns with an existing piece's open connector, "⚠ Won't connect" (this app's own existing invalid-tint styling, used in place of the design doc's literal grey-striped texture, which doesn't exist anywhere else in this codebase to reuse) when it's near existing track but not aligned, and always valid with no warning when it's starting a brand new line elsewhere on the map ("or it's the first piece of a new line," per the design doc). Track pieces also now sort into the existing Transportation → Trains catalog subcategory (previously only locomotive/tender/wagon did) via a `\brail\b` label-keyword match, verified not to catch "Railing A" or "Railroad Crossing."
  - **Not built this pass** (all explicitly optional/deferred per the design doc, not blockers to calling Trains genuinely driveable): a dedicated placeable "Station" marker/role, and the minimum-line-length/overlap-prevention refinements beyond what Build Mode's existing generic overlap check already provides.

- **2026-09-25, Boats Phase 2b (wake VFX + engine/splash SFX) and 2d (shared sound/reduced-motion toggle), teacher instruction "boats and other transportation."** `TownSquare.tsx`'s boat and car physics now feed a live 0-1 speed ratio and fire a soft contact "thud" (via a new `speedRef`/`soundRef` pair on `Player`, the same "write a ref every frame" pattern `facingRef` already used) into two new pieces:
  - **Wake VFX**: a new `VehicleTrailParticles` component, a small fixed pool (24) of flat billboard discs spawned behind the vehicle and faded/grown over a short lifetime, built exactly as `BOATS_DESIGN.md` §4 recommended — "a shared vehicle motion particle system... one system, two skins (dust vs. splash)." Only the `kind='wake'` skin is wired up this pass (Boats, this session's assigned scope); `kind='dust'` exists ready for Cars' own still-open dust trail (`DRIVING_UX_RESEARCH.md` rec #3) with no new pipeline needed when that gets picked up.
  - **Engine/splash SFX**: new `src/lib/vehicleAudio.ts`, a `VehicleSoundController` class synthesized entirely with the Web Audio API — **not a recorded audio asset**, because none exists: audited the full `public/sounds` tree before writing this and found only interface clicks, a cash register, a coin drop, a task-complete chime, and three ambient "calm" water sounds meant for the regulation tool (`bubbling-water.wav` etc, not a moving-vehicle SFX). This follows the exact same standing pattern `src/lib/chime.ts` already uses for a needed sound with no bundled recording (its own header comment: "Synthesized with the Web Audio API instead of a bundled audio file"), not a new one invented for this feature. Real, working, wired-up code — idle put-put, splash volume rising gently with speed, a soft dock/shore-contact thud, all exactly per `TRANSPORTATION.md` §4's "soft, loopable, never sudden-onset, crossfades in/out" rules — but genuinely synthesized rather than recorded, and **this sandbox cannot play audio to confirm it actually sounds calm rather than grating**, flagged plainly per this session's instructions: a human needs to listen to it in the real browser before calling it confirmed-good; if it's harsh, the fix is tuning the frequencies/filter cutoffs/gains in `vehicleAudio.ts`, not the wiring. Car engine sound was wired up in the same pass too (same controller class, `kind='car'`) even though it wasn't explicitly asked for this round, because 2d's own spec says the toggle is "needed for both Cars and Boats, not just Boats" — a toggle with nothing to mute for Cars would read as broken, and the controller already supported it at zero extra cost. Car dust-trail VFX was deliberately NOT added in the same pass (a separate, still-open, unassigned item).

Judgment call: the design doc's "reduced motion" half of this gap (`TRANSPORTATION.md` §7) is **not** a new field — `student.worldReduceMotion` already existed, already shipped, already respected elsewhere in this same file (the desk-glow motion fix), so the wake-particle trail and the "should this vehicle even have VFX motion" question both just check that existing toggle instead of adding a redundant second one. Reduce Motion suppresses the wake trail entirely (not just toned down) when it's on. SQL: `alter table students add column if not exists vehicle_sound_enabled boolean not null default true`.
