- **Gas gauge — rebuilt to a 10-dash, time-based, questions-only-refuel spec, refined across several direct teacher follow-ups, overriding this doc's earlier "never punitive/decorative-only" ruling.** **Note: the "10 correct in a row, any miss resets the streak to 0" mechanic described in this paragraph was superseded the same day — see "Question-set-gate pattern fixes... across the board" further down. The lockout is now a running total that never resets to 0 on a miss; only a brand-new lockout starting fresh begins at 0.** (Rest of this paragraph kept as accurate historical record of what was originally built.) Gas meter (10 dashes) drains 1 dash per **15** real seconds of driving/idling in a car (a full tank empties in exactly 150 seconds) — deliberately not gated on the gas pedal or on actually moving, just on being mounted — and persists across getting out of and back into the same car (`TownSquare.tsx`'s own state, not inside `Player`, so mount/dismount never resets it; only a fresh login does). The drain timer fully pauses (not just visually) the moment a gas question is on screen — voluntary Fill Up or the forced lockout alike — direct correction: "while answering questions to get more gas, the gas in the tank should be paused, and not decrease any more"; it resumes exactly where it left off once the modal closes. It only refills via correctly-answered questions at the gas pump: a real MC question at random from the teacher's own Question Sets library, +1 dash per correct (capped at 10), 0 for a wrong answer — no partial credit. Voluntary "Fill up" (gauge button, opens any time before empty) is optional and closable. If dashes hit 0 without refueling first, a blocking lockout opens automatically: student must answer 10 questions correct **in a row** (any miss resets the streak to 0) with no dismiss/skip/backdrop-close, before driving resumes — `gasBlocked` stops the car dead in `Player` while locked out. Claudia flagged streak-reset-to-0-on-a-miss as the single highest dysregulation-risk parameter in the mechanic for this population and named it on the record rather than silently softening it — kept exactly as specified at the teacher's explicit direction. Two mitigations Claudia did sign off on: a miss during lockout reads "Let's try the next one!" (never "streak reset"), and the running streak count stays visible ("You're at N of 10") through a miss. **No longer auto-tops-up when the library is empty — see the new auto-question generator entry below**, which now supplies a real fallback question instead. **`gas-pump` role, direct teacher request ("give asset role for gas pump")**: a teacher can place a model and assign it the Gas Pump role from Build Mode's role dropdown, same as Bank/Store/Cinema/etc; clicking a placed Gas Pump opens the exact same refuel prompt as the HUD's Fill Up button/the empty-tank lockout, right where the student is standing, instead of navigating to a 2D route (`ROLE_VIEWS['gas-pump']` is intentionally never read). Two models now carry this role: the catalog's existing "Gas Station" (`suburb` category) and a new teacher-uploaded, purpose-built "Gas Pump" model (also filed under `suburb`, `public/world/models/suburb/Gas_Pump.glb`) — a Sketchfab embed link she pasted first couldn't be used (view-only, no downloadable file, unverifiable license), so she exported and uploaded the real GLB directly instead. The HUD Fill Up button and the automatic empty-tank lockout both still work from anywhere while driving regardless of whether a pump is placed.
- **Steering fix — SHIPPED, direct teacher bug report ("right and left controls when driving are backwards").** Both the car and boat steer by incrementing `facing` directly rather than deriving it from a movement vector like walking does, and the sign was backwards — verified against the chase-cam math (`camAngle = facing`, screen-right = `-X` when `facing = 0`): pressing D/right was turning the nose left on screen. Fixed for both vehicles. Cars briefly picked up a reverse gear (Brake at a standstill reverses) per "model driving controls after Mario Kart," then the teacher corrected it in a follow-up: **"brake should not reverse. just stop the car."** Reversed back out — Brake now only ever decelerates a forward roll to a stop, `carSpeed` never goes negative, no reverse gear exists.
- **Collision: every placed object blocks movement now, not just role-having ones — direct teacher correction superseding the earlier trees/rocks-only fix.** First pass only added `forest` (trees/rocks) to `COLLIDING_CATEGORIES` for newly-placed objects; the teacher's follow-up was broader: "all assets that have a role... cannot be driven through, but currently the other assets can. fix so no assets can be driven or walked through." `TownSquare.tsx`'s collision-layout builder and `IslandBuild.tsx`'s obstacle list both now include every placed `worldObject` unconditionally — the `collides`/`role` gate is gone from the filter (the `collides` field itself stays in the data model, additive-only, just unread here now). This deliberately overrides the standing "never retroactively make an old object solid" guardrail from `types.ts`'s `collides` comment, since the teacher's instruction was explicit and general, not scoped to newly-placed objects. `HomeRoom.tsx`'s own room-collision list already had no such gate (every placed item already blocked movement there) — no change needed.
- **Achievements — paused entirely, direct teacher instruction: "clear all achievements, dont give anymore and dont add any without me saying it. that will be updated later."** `BADGES_PAUSED` (top of `store.ts`) is now `true`, and both `awardBadge` and `evaluateBadgeRules` are real no-ops while it's set — covers rule-based auto-awards AND the teacher's own manual Award button in Badge Manager (now disabled there with an explanatory banner, so it doesn't look like a silent bug). The existing `resetAllStudentAchievements()` action/button in Badge Manager (already built for a prior redesign) is how she actually clears every student's earned badges — this session didn't/couldn't invoke it directly (no live browser here), so it's still pending her own click. Standing instruction for future work in this file: do not add new entries to `DEFAULT_BADGES` (`./badges.ts`) without her asking for them specifically, and do not flip `BADGES_PAUSED` back without her explicit go-ahead to resume.

### Build Mode

- **Paint brush "acts as a bucket," walls unpaintable — fixed, direct teacher report.** Two real gaps found: (1) walls had zero participation in either paint tool at all (`if (paintMode) return; // walls don't participate in paint bucket/brush (no shared model to match on)`) — a click on a wall while painting silently did nothing, which reads as "broken," not "brush." `WallSegment.color` already existed as a field and `WallMesh` already rendered it as the base color, just nothing ever wrote to it — `paintNear` (Brush, radius-based) and a new `paintAllWalls` (Bucket) now cover walls the same way they already covered objects. (2) The "🌱 Ground texture" whole-map bucket-fill sat directly beside the actual radius-based Ground brush (`groundPatch` mode)'s own texture swatches, using an identical swatch-grid look — almost certainly what read as "the brush acts like a bucket," since it's a real one-click, no-radius, fills-everything action. Relabeled "🌱 Fill whole ground with this texture" with a comment pointing at the real 🖌️ Ground brush above it for an actual sized stroke; no behavior removed, just no longer visually indistinguishable from a brush. Floor objects (carpets etc.) already painted correctly through the existing object Brush/Bucket, since they're ordinary `WorldObject`s — no separate fix needed there.
- **Arbitrary texture-on-object painting:** DEFERRED. Today's tools recolor/retexture via tint or a preset ground/sky swap; true arbitrary UV re-texturing of any placed object was flagged early as a later, bigger pass.
- **HomeRoom.tsx's own size system — corrected this hour, not a straightforward fix.** Claudia's audit found the couch/bed/cabinet footprint/cube sizing is a direct, verbatim teacher instruction (`HomeRoom.tsx` lines 28-34), a protected decision, not a bug — `SIZE_REFERENCE.md` §3 previously implied it was an oversight and has been corrected. The real gap: `computeStarterScale` can only hit one target (length OR height) at once per item with today's single uniform `WorldObject.scale: number`, so it can't satisfy both of the teacher's own targets simultaneously the way she specified — fixing that for real needs per-axis (x/y/z) scale storage across every placed-object surface in the app (Town Square/Island/HomeRoom/sync alike), a real schema change, not a small fix. The genuinely open "1.0 = person height" gap is narrower than previously stated: really just the door/window class of items, not furniture sizing.
- **Native-game accessibility vetting:** POLICY DECIDED, TOOLING NOT BUILT. Currently the teacher's own judgment call at upload time; an automated pre-flight checklist could be worth building if volume grows.
- **YouTube duration auto-fetch:** WORKAROUND SHIPPED. Cinema shows a teacher-typed estimate for YouTube links since no YouTube Data API key is configured; uploads already auto-read real duration.
- **Stale `playgroundThreshold` field:** RETIRED from the app this hour. Confirmed it was truly dead (not read by `playgroundAccess.ts`'s real gating logic, and never exposed to the teacher in any editor), so it's been removed from `Student` (`types.ts`), the default new-student object (`store.ts`), and the sync layer's row mapping (`sync.ts`) rather than wired back in — the real unlock rule stays exactly the two paths it already was (both subjects done today, or a teacher-granted timed break). The `playground_threshold` column itself was left in place in `supabase/schema.sql` (unused, harmless) rather than dropped, matching this file's additive-only convention; no destructive DB change was made.
- **Clear All / Clear Room — SHIPPED across every build surface, direct teacher request ("give a clear room/clear all feature that deletes all assets").** Two-tap confirm (tap once to arm, tap again to actually delete — no browser `confirm()` dialog, matches this app's existing destructive-action pattern), never a single accidental tap. Town Square's Build Mode (`WorldEditor.tsx`) and Creative Island's Build mode (`IslandBuild.tsx`) both got a new toolbar "🗑️ Clear All" that deletes every placed object on that surface. Home Room (`HomeRoom.tsx`, already multi-room) got "🗑️ Clear Room" instead, scoped to just the currently active room — clearing one room doesn't touch a student's other rooms or their Yard, matching this file's own per-room model. None of these touch the fixed/original town layout (buildings, market stalls, road tiles) — only teacher/student-placed `WorldObject`s.
- **Creative Island live-mode lag — two safe, zero-visual-regression fixes shipped, direct teacher report.** (1) `IslandBuild.tsx`'s Canvas had `shadows` enabled and the light had `castShadow`, but nothing in the whole file ever sets `receiveShadow`/`castShadow` on an actual mesh (confirmed by search) — no shadow was ever visible, so the entire WebGL shadow-map subsystem was pure per-frame overhead for zero payoff. Removed. (2) Capped `dpr={[1, 1.5]}` on the Canvas to avoid rendering at full 2-3x retina pixel density on an iPad, the single biggest GPU fill-rate cost, and one that compounds with a large student-built object count (Island, unlike Town Square's smaller teacher-curated set, can accumulate a lot of props over a school year). Not fully profiled live (this environment can't run a browser) — flagged as best-effort; if lag persists, the likely next cause is the lack of instancing/batching across repeated placed models (every instance is its own draw call), a bigger follow-up pass, not attempted this session.
- **Fixed, direct teacher bug report: "cannot add role to assets (gas pump), it just closes the menu."** Root cause: the Role picker in the selected-object toolbar (`WorldEditor.tsx`) was a native `<select>` inside a drei `<Html>` overlay on top of the WebGL canvas. A native select's open dropdown renders as OS/browser chrome outside that overlay's own DOM — so the pointerup/click that dismisses it (picking an option) lands back on the canvas underneath at the same screen coordinates, hits the ground plane's own click handler, and deselects the whole object, closing the toolbar before the role change is even visible. Same root cause Claudia's earlier focus-group audit already flagged and fixed for the category filter dropdown in this same file. Fixed the same way: replaced the native select with a same-DOM scrollable button list (matches the tint-swatch picker's own pattern), which can't trigger a stray canvas click.
- **Fixed, direct teacher bug report: "items should be solid on default."** Root cause, Home Room only (Town Square and Creative Island were already universal): `roomObstacles` only ever built a collision entry for a placed object whose model matched the fixed starter/yard `CATALOG_ITEMS` list — a purchased Marketplace furniture item (built for the Marketplace furniture pass above) was never in that list, so it had zero collision, walkable straight through, with no flag anywhere a teacher could set to fix it. Every placed Home Room object gets a real obstacle now regardless of catalog membership — a catalog match still uses its real target-size radius, anything else (marketplace furniture, any future item type) falls back to a generic scale-based radius, matching the "never silently non-solid" rule Town Square/Island's own object collision already follows.
- **Fixed, direct teacher bug report: "students can go through them a little bit and get stuck," now fixed on all three world surfaces (Town Square, Creative Island, Home Room).** Root cause: each surface's movement-collision function only ever checked whether the TARGET point of a move was inside an obstacle; if the CURRENT point ever ended up inside one (two objects placed close enough to overlap, a frame hiccup, a fast vehicle covering more ground in one frame than a walking student), every fallback path bottomed out at "don't move," with no way to ever get back out — a permanent stuck-touching-the-obstacle state. Fixed the same way everywhere: push straight back out to the nearest obstacle's edge first, so "current position" is never itself an invalid one to fall back to, before evaluating the requested move — the same stateless push-out shape `blockBuildings` already used safely for the fixed town buildings.
- **Fixed, direct teacher bug report: navigation icons "highlighting" and breaking driving/walking on a touch screen.** The D-pad, drive Gas/Brake pedals, and camera-look buttons are all hold-to-move controls (`onPointerDown`/`onPointerUp`), but each rendered a visible text caption (and the pedals, an emoji) inside the button. On iOS Safari, holding down on rendered text/emoji content triggers the native Copy/Look Up text-selection callout mid-hold, which broke the gesture the student was actively doing. Fixed two ways: the visible captions are gone (icon-only now, matching every other control in this app, with the accessible name moved to `aria-label`; the Gas/Brake pedals now use the same non-text rotated-arrow icon the D-pad already uses instead of an emoji), and every one of these buttons now also sets `WebkitTouchCallout`/`WebkitUserSelect`/`userSelect: none` directly, closing the callout for good regardless of what content ever ends up inside them.
- **Confirmed already working, direct teacher requirement: "gas pumps can be utilized while driving (no exit car needed)."** Audited the full click path — a gas pump's `onClick` handler (`obj.role && !mapView ? () => setSelectedRoleObjectId(obj.id) : ...`) has no dependency on `drivingObjectId` anywhere in the ternary, and neither does `openRoleObject`'s own `gas-pump` special case. Clicking a placed Gas Pump while driving a car already opens the same "⛽ Get gas?" confirm card and refuel quiz it does on foot — no code change needed, confirmed by reading, not assumed.

### Auto-generated fallback questions

- **SHIPPED (partial, by design), direct teacher instruction: "auto questions should be things like, select the correct spelling pattern (grab ufli scope), answer the multiplication or division fact, complete the subtraction or addition equation, define the word based on the morphemes. lets start with this only."** New `src/lib/autoQuestions.ts`: a generated (not teacher-authored) pool of real MC questions, shaped exactly like `MCQuestion` so anything already able to render one can use it. Four generator types shipped: addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division facts (numbers 1-12, always whole-number results, no per-student grade targeting since none exists in the data model — kept simple per "lets start with this only"), and morpheme-based word definitions, built from the existing hand-verified `morphology.ts` affix-meaning list and `morphemeContent.ts` word set (e.g. "careless" → "without care", composed literally from the real parts, not a polished dictionary definition — that's the actual point of a morpheme exercise). **Spelling-pattern-by-UFLI-scope was NOT built.** Same standing rule as the UFLI blending board entry above: this environment has no way to fetch or verify the real published UFLI scope-and-sequence, and "grab ufli scope" isn't something achievable from here — inventing a plausible-looking sequence and presenting it as UFLI-grounded would be a real instructional-accuracy risk for exactly the students this serves. Needs the teacher to actually supply the real document (same upload pattern the Sentence Formulas curriculum reference used) before this fifth type can be built for real; the module is written so it slots in as a fifth generator with no other changes once that exists. **Wired into one consumer so far:** the gas-refuel loop's `pickGasQuestion` now falls back to `generateAutoQuestion()` instead of silently auto-topping-up the tank when the teacher's Question Sets library has no MC content — a student always gets a real question now, never a free pass and never a broken prompt. Not wired anywhere else yet; the module is written generically (plain exported functions returning `MCQuestion`) specifically so it can be reused elsewhere without rework, if asked.

### Global background music player

- **SHIPPED, direct teacher instruction: "ensure that the music player can always be played in the background, even when students are completing assignments. the music player should have a minimized view."** Previously the entire player (the hidden YouTube audio iframe, the Spotify-style transport bar) lived inside `TownSquare.tsx` and died the instant a student navigated to a task/quiz screen — the exact opposite of "background." Moved to a new `src/components/GlobalMusicPlayer.tsx`, mounted once in `App.tsx` alongside `TeacherHelpAlert`/`CoinDropOverlay`/etc. so it survives every route change; `playingTrackId` itself moved from `TownSquare.tsx` local state into the store (`store.ts`, session-only, not persisted to localStorage) for the same reason. Deliberately kept outside `routes/world/` and importing nothing from `@react-three/fiber` — Three.js stays lazy-loaded for world routes only, per `App.tsx`'s own existing comment on that split; a component mounted for every route can't pull that in. New minimized view: a small "now playing" pill, bottom-left, that never blocks a task/quiz's own content; tapping it expands the existing full transport bar (seek/volume/prev/next/stop), tapping ▾ re-minimizes. Town Square still owns picking a track (the radio/Concert Hall/Boom Box triggers, and the track-browser picker UI) — it just calls the shared `setPlayingTrackId` action instead of owning playback itself.
- **Fixed, direct teacher bug report: "won't let me switch between songs."** Root cause was a missing React `key` on the hidden YouTube-embed component — without one, changing tracks reused the SAME `<iframe>` DOM node (React just updated its id/src), but the outgoing track's own cleanup still calls the YouTube Player API's `destroy()`, which physically removes that iframe from the DOM. That ripped out the very node React had just repointed at the new track, a beat before the new track's effect could look it up by id and attach a player to it — so Next/Prev (and picking a brand new song) silently did nothing once you weren't on the very first track anymore. `key={ytId}` now forces a real unmount/remount per track: the old track's own, no-longer-reused iframe gets destroyed cleanly, and the new track gets its own fresh one. Confirmed already correct and unchanged: the radio is part of the car, so exiting a driven vehicle already calls `setPlayingTrackId(null)` and stops the music (direct teacher ask, already shipped).

Buying one (`buyMarketplaceItem`, and free-grants via `grantFreeMarketplaceItem`) adds it to the new `Student.ownedHomeItemIds`. `HomeRoom.tsx`'s catalog now merges in every purchasable furniture item alongside the existing free `STARTER_ITEMS`: owned ones are placeable exactly like any starter item (same scale-calibration pipeline, extended to cover them too); unowned ones show locked (🔒 + "Buy in Marketplace", tapping opens the Marketplace) rather than being hidden, per the Pet Shelter precedent Claudia's intake named. Fixed in the same pass: a real 🛋️ Home tab (search/category filter, the same buyable-item-card pattern Fonts/Voices/Prizes already use) now exists in `Marketplace.tsx`, and `ownedFieldFor`/`renderBuyableItem` there were extended to recognize the `furniture` kind. ### Computer as a real dashboard — webpage-frame standard, Bank/Cinema/Chat widgets

- Kayden's own words, with two reference images (a laptop-bezel mockup of the current computer screen, and a collage of retro Cartoon Network/Nick.com-style web portals plus an OS-window-chrome reference sheet): "i want the coputer screen to look more like attatche image one, where the student can see the computer as if it was a frame for the current view... think of accessing thier computer as the main view and a dashboard to access everything related ot the game that the studnet can interact with. Bank should look like a webpage, with a widget of a chart of their current account. cinema should have a widget. chat should have a webpage looking widget like looks like an old IM page. claudia should take this idea and apply it to all parts of this function"
- Spec: a shared `WebpageFrame` component (title bar, traffic lights, fake address bar showing the real route as a URL, one Back button in the same position on every screen) replacing each screen's own bespoke header, starting with Bank, Marketplace, Mailbox. Three new Computer-desktop widgets, all built on real existing data, nothing fabricated: a Bank sparkline reusing `PiggyBankCharts.tsx`'s already-real balance-history derivation, a Cinema poster-tile widget (most recent or favorited video, static, no autoplay), and an IM-styled Chat widget reusing `ChatPanel.tsx`'s real message data. See A42 for what's already shipped underneath this (the widget-desktop grid itself).
- **SHIPPED this pass.** `WebpageFrame.tsx` built and applied to StudentHome (computer), Mailbox, and Piggy Bank (Marketplace still pending, bundled with its own larger redesign below). Bank widget now shows a real sparkline (`bankDayTotals`, same per-day running-balance derivation `PiggyBankCharts.tsx` uses, just unlabeled and small) plus the live balance — no fabricated history. New Cinema widget shows the real most-recently-added video's real thumbnail (teacher's own `coverImageUrl` or the real YouTube auto-thumbnail), static, no autoplay, "Now Showing." Chat widget shows the real last message in the student's own thread, styled as a small IM-window nested inside the widget-card (`.widget-webpage`/`.widget-card-tall` in `index.css`) — no fabricated unread count, since no read/unread field exists on `ChatMessage` yet.
- **Claudia's code review, fixed same pass:** (1) the Back button had an inline `minHeight: 32` overriding `.btn-sm`'s standard 44px touch target on every `WebpageFrame` screen — removed, the class default applies everywhere now. (2) Collapsing Mailbox/PiggyBank/Marketplace to one Back button lost the old "walked up to this building in Town Square, tap Back, land back in Town Square" path (they all defaulted to the Computer instead) — `TownSquare.tsx`'s own navigation into these screens now passes `state: { from: 'town' }`, which `WebpageFrame` reads to send Back to Town Square instead of the Computer when that's really where the student came from; a caller with its own explicit `backTo` (the Computer's own "Close, back to Town Square") is unaffected. (3) The Bank widget's balance text (`--success` green on white) and the Chat widget's sender label (`--blue` on a light blue bubble) both failed WCAG AA contrast — darkened to `#16803c` and `#1e4fa8`. **SHIPPED, laptop bezel — now on every `WebpageFrame` screen, direct teacher follow-up ("do the laptop-bezel redesign for all webpage screens").** `.laptop-frame`/`.laptop-screen`/`.laptop-deck` in `index.css` originally wrapped only the Computer screen (StudentHome.tsx) in a real physical laptop mockup (dark bezel + keyboard deck) matching the teacher's reference image. Extended this pass to the other three `WebpageFrame` call sites — `PiggyBank.tsx`, `Mailbox.tsx`, `Marketplace.tsx` — reusing the exact same three CSS classes rather than inventing new styling, so all four screens read identically. Decorative only, no interaction; `.laptop-screen`'s `overflow: hidden` only clips content bleeding past its rounded corners (it has no fixed/max height, so it never actually truncates a long page like Marketplace's or Piggy Bank's scrollable history), and every fixed-position modal/FAB still escapes the bezel exactly as before, since neither wrapper div sets a `transform`. **Still not done (at the time):** Cinema/Chat/Arcade/Gallery/Farmers Market/Silly Quizzes don't use `WebpageFrame` at all (different chrome patterns each), so they're outside this mechanism unless asked for specifically.
- **SHIPPED (2026-09-25), the rest of the rollout — direct teacher instruction: "computer dashboard continuation."** All six screens the note above flagged as outside the mechanism now use `WebpageFrame` and the `.laptop-frame`/`.laptop-screen`/`.laptop-deck` bezel the same way Mailbox/PiggyBank/Marketplace already did — Cinema, Arcade, Gallery, and Farmer's Market (`Cinema.tsx`/`Arcade.tsx`/`Gallery.tsx`/`FarmersMarket.tsx`), each keeping its own real content untouched (Cinema's curtain-photo backdrop and percentage-positioned video overlay, Arcade's Scratch shelf/embed, Gallery's tap-to-enlarge grid, Farmer's Market's trade board) underneath the new shared chrome. Back-button routing is unregressed: Cinema/Arcade/Farmer's Market are real Town Square roles (`ROLE_VIEWS` in `townLayout.ts`), so `WebpageFrame`'s existing from-town/from-Computer default (the `state: { from: 'town' }` mechanism above) covers them automatically with no extra code, exactly like Mailbox/PiggyBank did; Gallery and Silly Quizzes have no Town Square building at all (verified in `PlaygroundView.tsx` — they're only ever reached from the Playground), so both pass an explicit `backTo="/student/playground/view"` instead of falling through to the Computer default, preserving what their old three-button header already did. Silly Quizzes (`SillyQuizzes.tsx`) got the same treatment. **Chat is the one adaptation, not a straight port:** `ChatPanel.tsx` is a shared teacher/student overlay modal opened from six different call sites (Student Home, Help overlay, the student/teacher chat alerts, Teacher Home, Student Live View), not a routed page, so wrapping it in the full `.laptop-frame` bezel or a router-based Back button would have broken every one of those callers' `onClose` contracts. Instead, `WebpageFrame` gained an optional `onBack` prop — when passed, the Back button calls it directly instead of navigating, leaving every routed screen's existing `backTo` behavior untouched. `ChatPanel` now opens with `<WebpageFrame url={chatUrl} onBack={onClose} backLabel="✕ Close" />` in place of its old plain dark title bar, with the fake address bar itself doing double duty as the "who is this thread with" identifier (`chat/kayden` for a teacher's view of a student's thread, `chat/teacher` for the student's own side) — a real "looks like an old IM page" touch, per the teacher's original wording, that a plain title bar didn't have. **Re-checked against the original spec paragraph for anything not marked SHIPPED, per direct instruction:** all three Computer-desktop widgets it asked for (Bank sparkline, Cinema poster-tile, IM-styled Chat preview) were already marked SHIPPED above and independently verified still wired to real data in `StudentHome.tsx` (`bankDayTotals`, `latestVideoCover`, `lastChatMessage`) — there was nothing outstanding to build here; the "two widgets" framing in that follow-up request didn't match what's actually still open in this section.

### Marketplace — teacher earn-source editing + Amazon-style browse

- Kayden's own words: "marketplace needs to evolve. as a teacher, in game tab, i need full ability to edit all prices, avaibility windows and resons for earning, etc. for everyting marketplace related. the design needs to be more real onlline shoping inspired, have a search, etc. marketplace needs to be like amazon, still having a website frame that wil be standard and applied to all 'webpages'"
- Spec: new `earnMethods?: EarnMethod[]` field on `MarketplaceItem` ('purchase' | 'daily-spin' | 'bonus-spin' | 'quest-reward' | 'farmers-market'), edited as a chip multi-select per item in `MarketplaceManager.tsx`. Existing items default to all wheel-eligible values on migration (matches today's real unfiltered-pool behavior, no regression); new items default to purchase-only until the teacher opts them into a wheel. `dailySpin.ts`'s segment generator gets a real filter on this field for the first time (today it draws from the entire item list with no eligibility check at all). Characters and Emotes get brought into the same editable price/availability table the other item kinds already have (today Characters have zero per-item editing, Emotes only has a price override). Student-facing redesign: real search bar, keep the existing category chips, oversized "Add to cart" buttons, wrapped in the same `WebpageFrame` standard as the rest of the Computer. **Settled, won't build:** star ratings, written reviews, "customers also bought" cross-sell — real Amazon patterns that either open an unsupervised peer-content surface or add manipulative purchase pressure this population doesn't need; left out deliberately, not by oversight.
- **SHIPPED this pass, the data-model half + Characters pricing + a real search.** `MarketplaceItem.earnMethods` (types.ts) plus `EARN_METHOD_LABELS`/`earnMethodsFor`/`itemEarnsVia` (`marketplaceSeed.ts`) are real now — `MarketplaceManager.tsx`'s `EarnMethodChips` lets a teacher toggle any item between Purchase only/Daily Spin/Bonus Spin/Quest reward/Farmer's Market per item, and `dailySpin.ts`'s segment pool now actually filters on it (`itemEarnsVia(it, 'daily-spin')`) instead of drawing from every eligible item unconditionally like it always has. Characters got the exact override-map treatment Emotes already had (`avatarPriceOverrides`/`setAvatarPriceOverride`, new `CharacterPricesSettings` panel) — a real bug was caught and fixed while wiring this in: `buyAvatar` in `store.ts` was charging the raw hardcoded catalog price even before this pass, ignoring any override entirely (unlike `buyEmote`, which already read from its override map) — now fixed, so a teacher-set Character price is the price actually charged, not just the price shown. A real search box (Characters/Emotes/Power-Ups tabs, which had none; Fonts/Voices/Prizes already had their own via `ItemFilterBar`) and `WebpageFrame` now wrap `Marketplace.tsx`. **Not yet done (at the time):** the full Amazon-style layout pass (sidebar categories, bigger product-grid treatment) — today's category-chip tab row was kept as-is per the "it already works, don't reinvent it" guidance, so what shipped is closer to "search added + one shared frame" than a visual redesign; that's still open if the teacher wants the fuller Amazon look.
- **SHIPPED (2026-09-25), the full Amazon-style layout pass — direct teacher instruction: "marketplace" (continuing the request above).** A real left-hand sidebar (`.shop-sidebar` in `index.css`) replaces the old chip-tab row as the category nav (Characters/Emotes/Writing/Whiteboard/Voices/Prizes/Power-Ups/Home/Pets/My Stuff/Receipts) — same `tab` state and click handlers as before, just rendered as a vertical nav instead of wrapped pills, and it collapses to a horizontal row under 720px so it still works at phone width. Every product tile (`.shop-product-grid`/`.shop-product-card`, new classes) moved off the old loose flex-wrap onto a real CSS grid (`repeat(auto-fill, minmax(168px, 1fr))`) with uniform card sizing — the several places that used to hardcode a one-off card width per item kind (140/150/156px for characters/emotes/powerups) now all size from the same grid track, a genuinely more "product grid" look than before. The buy button on every tile is now a full-width, oversized "🛒 Add to Cart · $price" button (`.shop-add-to-cart-btn`, 48px tall) in place of the old small rounded price chip, with the same green "in cart"/disabled-when-unaffordable states as before, still wrapped in the same `WebpageFrame` + laptop bezel from the earlier pass. The existing search box and every `ItemFilterBar` category/tag dropdown (Fonts/Voices/Prizes/Furniture) are untouched — nothing about the working filter functionality was removed, only the outer chrome around it. **Deliberately scoped to Marketplace only, not the shared classes:** `PetShelter.tsx` and `PetJournal.tsx` also render with `.shop-item-grid`/`.shop-item-card`/`.shop-price-chip`/`.shop-panel`/`.shop-header`/`.shop-ribbon`/`.shop-balance-chip`/`.shop-item-icon-frame` — all of those original classes were left completely untouched, and `Marketplace.tsx` was switched onto brand-new sibling classes (`shop-product-grid`/`shop-product-card`/`shop-add-to-cart-btn`/`shop-sidebar`/`shop-main`/`shop-layout`) instead of redefining the shared ones, specifically so this redesign can't leak into the Pet system's screens, which other agents own. **Reaffirmed, not revisited:** star ratings, written reviews, and "customers also bought" cross-sell stay out, per the "Settled, won't build" line above — nothing in this pass added any comparative or peer-visible signal to a product tile.

### Bakery Match — question-gated match-3 mini-game (Town Square)

*(Renamed from "Bakery" to "Bakery Match" 2026-09-25, per the round-2 build entry below — "Bakery" is the building/location, "Bakery Match" is the game students play inside it.)*

- **SHIPPED (2026-09-25), new building/location — direct teacher instruction: "i want to do a candy crush like game but bakery theme with a bakery building asset i will upload," plus a same-day follow-up adding a post-game treat wheel with a pet-feeding tie-in.** The first of the "mini games embedded with question set logic" concept (car/gas, cafe were her illustrative examples, not literal asks) to actually ship, chosen because match-3 was the concrete, scoped one. A new `WorldObjectRole` (`'bakery'`) lets a teacher assign any placed object the same way she already assigns Bank/Cinema/Gas Pump — `ROLE_VIEWS.bakery = '/student/bakery'` routes through the existing generic `openRoleObject` navigation in `TownSquare.tsx`, so no special-cased click handling was needed (unlike Gas Pump's in-world modal). Her own uploaded 3D building (`Bakery_by_Poly_by_Google_-...glb`, same "Poly by Google" CC-BY source already used for Cinema/Windmill/etc. elsewhere in this world) is in `public/world/models/buildings/bakery.glb`, auto-discovered by the Asset Directory's build-time manifest scan — she places it and assigns the role herself in Build Mode, same as any other building.
- **Match-3 engine, `src/lib/matchThree.ts` — a from-scratch, clean-room implementation** (grid init that avoids pre-existing runs, horizontal/vertical run-of-3+ detection, adjacent-swap validation, gravity/cascade clear-and-refill, valid-move check with a silent reshuffle instead of a "stuck board" dead end) written against the publicly-documented match-3 mechanics, not copied from any reference project — keeps this platform's standing rule (GPL/AGPL reference-only, nothing copied in) clean with zero licensing string attached.
- **`src/routes/student/BakeryMatch3.tsx` — free-play, not an assigned Task.** Question-sourcing follows the Gas Pump pattern exactly (`TownSquare.tsx`'s `gasQuestionPool`), not Platformer's Task-mastery-queue pattern: a random MC question pulled from the whole teacher Question Sets library, falling back to `generateAutoQuestion()` when empty. A question break pops up every 4 cleared match-groups, non-punitive framing throughout ("💛 Not quite! Let's keep baking" — never "wrong"), correct answers add a small coin bonus but a miss never costs anything or blocks continued play. Matched tiles pay real Class Cash via `recordTransaction` at the same `CENTS_PER_COIN = 5` rate Platformer uses, settled either when the student clicks "Finish Baking & Spin" or, as a safety net, on unmount if they navigate away mid-game. Wrapped in `WebpageFrame` + the `.laptop-frame` bezel, matching the now-platform-wide "webpage" convention with zero special-casing needed (it's a real `ROLE_VIEWS` entry, so the from-town/from-Computer Back routing just works).
- **Tile art and SFX are teacher-provided commercial assets, not emoji placeholders** (the original plan) — she uploaded real art before the placeholder was ever shipped. Six treats (croissant/donut/muffin/pretzel/loaf/cinnamon roll) from her purchased "Bakery Asset Pack v1.1" (itch.io, jimal-art — commercial-use license, attribution requested: credit jimal-art.itch.io) live in `public/bakery/tiles/`; four SFX (match/combo/fail/pop) from her "Triple Treat SFX" pack live in `public/sounds/bakery/`. A separate CC0 "Tiny Treats Baked Goods" 3D pack she also uploaded (Isa Lousberg, isalousberg.com) was not used — it's FBX/OBJ/glTF 3D models, and the wheel/tiles only need flat 2D icons, which the commercial pack already provided; kept in mind as a future option if she wants an actual 3D treat model rather than a flat icon somewhere.
- **Post-game treat wheel, `src/components/BakeryTreatWheel.tsx` — direct follow-up instruction: "when the game is completed, the student should have a wheel spin (same as daily and bonus wheels) with only these bakery treat options. players can eat these and they can give them to their pets. if they give them to their pets, their food bar will increase one notch."** Reuses the same `spin-wheel` library and visual shape as `DailySpinWheel.tsx`, trimmed to just the six Bakery treats at equal odds (no cash economy — this wheel is a bonus flourish, not another income source). "The game is completed" reads as ambiguous for an endless free-play board with no level/win condition, so it's resolved as the student's own call: a "🎡 Finish Baking & Spin for a Treat!" button appears once they've earned any coins this visit, settles the coin payout, then opens the wheel. After landing on a treat, two real choices, both wired to existing systems rather than a new inventory layer: **"🍽️ Eat it!"** just closes out the moment (flavor, not mechanical — she didn't ask for an eating effect); **"🐾 Give to a pet"** lists the student's own owned pets (`StudentPet[]` filtered by `studentId`) and, on pick, calls the pet system's existing `carePet(petId, 'feed')` action — already built with exactly the food/social/health-bar system this ask needed (`StudentPet.food`, 0-100, soft floor, never punished by absence), so "food bar increases one notch" is `carePet`'s existing `+25` feed amount, zero new store/schema work required.
- **Round 2, SHIPPED (2026-09-25) — direct teacher instruction: rounds/challenge screens, the dice-vs-dropdown question-source pattern, a 100-question tracker, and a Cake Character unlock.** Four real asks bundled into one pass:
  - **Rounds + Challenge Screen** ("show a little challenge screen between each round of the game, think candy crush levels for the length of each round"). The board is now structured into rounds — round *N* needs `5 + (N-1)×2` cleared match-groups (5, 7, 9, 11…, a little longer each round, like a level getting harder) — with **no move limit and no fail state**, consistent with this platform's standing non-punitive design (no lives, nothing to lose). Hitting the target freezes the board and opens the Challenge Screen ("🎉 Round N Complete!"), which is also where the question-set-gated question now lives — replacing the earlier mid-board "every 4 matches" interrupt with one question at the natural checkpoint a level-complete moment already is. Answering (right or wrong, non-punitive either way) unlocks "Start Round N+1"; the board itself carries over between rounds rather than resetting.
  - **Question-source picker, `src/components/QuestionSourcePicker.tsx`** — direct teacher instruction: "students have a few options 1) they can select a dice icon and have a dice spin random... drawing randomly from all of their assigned question sets 2) they can select from a dropdown menu for their questions to draw from their current focuses." Built as a small reusable component (first used here, meant for any future question-set-gated game): a 🎲 button (random, pooled across every teacher question set, the existing Gas Pump-style behavior) and a 📋 dropdown of the individual Question Sets library (there's no direct data link from a `QuestionSet` to the separate `Focus` "current focus" concept today, so "current focuses" is read as "pick a specific one of your question sets" rather than the wordlist-only `Focus` type, which has no MC-question content to draw from). Shown once before Round 1 (a "How do you want your questions?" start screen) and again on every Challenge Screen, so the choice is a standing option through the whole session, not a one-time setting.
  - **Bakery Match tracker** — `Student.bakeryQuestionsAnswered` (new, additive, default 0 — `types.ts`/`sync.ts`/`schema.sql`), incremented by the new `recordBakeryQuestionAnswered` store action every time a Challenge Screen question is answered, right or wrong ("a tracker for every question answered," not a mastery-only count). Shown as a small "🏆 N/100 questions answered" pill in the game's header at all times.
  - **Cake Character unlock, `src/lib/characterCatalog.ts`** — direct teacher instruction: "if the student answers 100 questions in the Bakery Match game specifically, they will earn the ability to upgrade their character to this cake character. ensure it uses the human player assets for movement and animations. it cant just have its arms out." Crossing 100 adds `'cake'` to a new `Student.unlockedCharacterIds` array and bumps a new transient `lastCharacterUnlock` store field (same shape/purpose as the existing `lastCoinEarn` trigger), which the Bakery Match screen watches to show a one-time "🎂 You unlocked the Cake Character!" celebration with an Equip/Later choice; a small header button lets the student re-equip any time after. **The technical constraint the teacher's own warning anticipated, confirmed directly by reading the uploaded GLB's own glTF JSON**: her uploaded Cake Character model is a completely static, unrigged single mesh (0 skins, 0 animation clips of its own) — animating it can't come from the file itself. `TownSquare.tsx`'s `PlayerModel` was extended with a `CharacterSkinOverlay`: the default player model's own cloned skeleton and idle/walk `AnimationClip`s (`/world/models/characters/player.glb`) stay exactly as they are — its two default body meshes are hidden, and the Cake mesh is rigidly parented onto the skeleton's `'torso'` bone specifically because that's the one bone both the idle clip (a subtle rotation sway) and the walk clip (root-driven bob it inherits, plus its own rotation) actually animate, so the Cake visibly sways and bobs with the same motion instead of sitting frozen in a bind pose — an honest "rigid mascot" look (no separate limb articulation, since the source mesh has no limbs), not the broken "arms out" T-pose the instruction warned against. This is a genuinely new character-catalog system (`equipCharacter`/`equippedCharacterId`, also new/additive on `Student`), not a one-off hack — `CHARACTER_CATALOG` in `characterCatalog.ts` is built to hold more skins later. The skin model lives in `public/world/character-skins/` (deliberately *outside* `public/world/models/`, which is auto-scanned into the teacher's Build Mode Asset Directory — a character skin isn't a placeable world object). **Needs a live teacher look, same standing caveat as every 3D change in this doc**: the skin's auto-computed scale/position (a bounding-box height match against an eyeballed torso-to-head-top span, since this sandbox cannot render WebGL/Three.js to check by eye) is a reasoned estimate, not a verified fit.
- **Round 3, SHIPPED (2026-09-25) — direct teacher instruction, three messages in a row plus a full rules rewrite ("update game play logic immediately"), superseding round 2's webpage shell, coin economy, and round-target formula above.** Two halves, shipped together as one rewrite since the rules message landed mid-build on the shell/UI half:

Each formula is a color-coded slot row (WHO=yellow, ACTION=green, WHAT=red, WHERE=magenta, WHEN=orange, DESCRIPTION=cyan) ending in a `. ! ?` punctuation-choice column, with worked examples using her own real names and pets (Mom, Dad, "Ms. Kayden," Xander, Geoff, Azalea the cat, Yoga — her own comic character, referenced elsewhere as "Yoga Comic Sentence Formulas") — not generic placeholder names. Word banks are explicitly leveled by phonics stage (a "General" bank, then separate CVC and VCe word banks per slot color) so the same formula can be practiced at an easier or harder decoding level, something the app's phonics-agnostic word lists don't do today. Two blank template layouts exist (Horizontal grid, Vertical grid) plus a linked "Flippity Randomizer" (an external randomizer tool, not something to build in-app — the app's own randomize-a-sentence mechanic already covers that need). A later page ("Question words, articles, conjunctions") shows a harder, silly-sentence tier using her Yoga-comic-universe characters and invented nonsense nouns ("gurgle wurple," "Squirellanida") — a real example of the exact "expanded to ensure high quality" content tier Claudia's discovery document's Question A/F (licensing, grade range) should account for, since this tier is 100% her own original content with zero licensing question, unlike the DSF morpheme material.
  - **Montessori Grammar Symbols — two reference sheets read directly (images pasted into chat, not blocked links).** Level 1: 9 symbols (black triangle=noun, small blue triangle=article, dark blue triangle=adjective, red circle=verb, green crescent=preposition, orange circle=adverb, purple triangle=pronoun, pink rectangle=conjunction, gold cone/teardrop=interjection), each with a full definition and example words — this is the real, standard Montessori grammar-symbol set (large red circle for verb, black triangle for noun, etc. are the actual internationally-standard shapes/colors, not something invented for this request). Level 2 adds 9 more refined subtypes (proper/collective/abstract/spiritual noun variants on the black-triangle noun shape; transitive/intransitive/linking/auxiliary verb variants on the red-circle verb shape; infinitive, participle, gerund) as shape/color only, no definitions given yet.
  - **Montessori "predictable sentence frames" — two example images read directly.** A grammar-symbol-tagged sentence ("Walk down the hallway." / "She dances and sings beautifully." / "He ate on the table." / "A fuzzy cat sleeps.") is followed immediately by its own symbol-tile version directly below it (the same words' shapes/colors, no text, laid out as a strip) — the symbol strip functions as a wordless "parse" of the sentence directly above it, letting a student match words to grammar roles without reading comprehension being the bottleneck. A second image shows a physical (photographed, not digital) version of the same idea for conjunctions specifically: real word cards ("the green crayon," "and," "the red crayon") laid out under matching grammar-symbol shapes, with real crayons placed underneath as the concrete referent — "the green crayon AND the red crayon" / "the yellow crayon OR the blue crayon," teaching a conjunction by physically pairing two concrete objects rather than an abstract definition alone.

Direct instruction: "these dark blue shapes... need to be removed. it should not be there at all." **`EquirectangularReflectionMapping` is now confirmed broken by a real live look on two independent source images in this codebase (the 4th attempt's Kenney skybox and this 6th attempt's teacher-uploaded images) — this is a standing rule, not a per-image one: do not retry this mapping technique again on a new image, in either `TownSquare.tsx` or `WorldEditor.tsx`.** Full removal, not just hiding: `SkyboxTexture`/`BuildSkyTexture`/`SKY_TEXTURE_OPTIONS`/`SkyTextureBoundary.tsx` (the fallback error boundary built for this feature) are all deleted from both files; Town Square and Build Mode's Fill Sky panel now always render a single flat `THREE.Color`, full stop, regardless of what's stored in `app_settings.sky_texture` — the column itself stays in `schema.sql` (additive-only, never dropped) but is never read for rendering again.
